**Makkī** (revealed in Mecca); it has 597 letters, 139 words, and 30 verses.

Nāfil ibn Rāqim ibn Aḥmad al-Bābī informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Sādah narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the sūrah *Wal-Fajr* during the ten nights [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], he will be forgiven; and whoever recites it on the remaining days, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." [139] [[Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān: 10/341.]]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ (By the dawn). Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means the entire day. ʿAṭiyyah reported from him: the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). ʿUthmān ibn Muḥṣin reported from him: the dawn of Muharram. Qatādah said likewise: it is the first day of Muharram, from which the year bursts forth. Ḍaḥḥāk: the dawn of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, because Allah, glorified is He, joined the days to it. ʿIkrimah and Zayd ibn Aslam: the morning (al-ṣubḥ). Muqātil: it refers to the dawn of every year in its entirety. al-Qurẓī: the breaking of dawn from every day until the end of the world. In some tafsīrs: *al-Fajr* refers to the rocks and springs from which water bursts forth.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ (and ten nights). Mujāhid, Qatādah, Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and al-Ḥalabī said: they are the ten [nights] of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. ʿIkrimah: the nights of the Ḥajj. Masrūq said: they are the best days of the year. Abū Rawq, from Ḍaḥḥāk: they are the first ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, said: they are the last ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Yamān ibn Rabāb: the first ten [nights] of Muharram, of which the tenth is the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.

Akhbarani al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Ḥamdān narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Isḥāq al-Anṣārī narrated to us, saying: Manjāb ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmārah informed us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ḥassān narrated to us, from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, concerning His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾. He said: It is the dawn that you know. I said: ﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾? He said: The ten of al-Aḍḥā. I said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾? He said: its creation, as Allah says: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾. I said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾? He said: Allah is the Odd (witr). I said to him: Do you narrate this ḥadīth from any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. I said: From whom? He said: From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [140] [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 30/214; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 20/40.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Naṣrawayh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and ʿAbdah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, both saying: Abū al-Ḥusayn Zayd ibn al-Ḥubbāb al-ʿUklī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbās ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, saying: Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr wa Layālin ʿAshr﴾, said:

"[It is] the ten of sacrifice (al-naḥr); and the odd (witr) is the Day of ʿArafah; and the even (shaf') is the Day of Sacrifice." [141] [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/445.]]

And with the same chain, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Maslamah al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: Wāṣil ibn al-Sāʾib al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, saying: Abū Sawdah narrated to me, saying: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾. He said: "The even (shaf') is the Day of ʿArafah and the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and the odd (witr) is the night of sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr)." [142] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/238.]]

And Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Faḍl al-Fahandarī informed us, saying: Abū al-Ṭāhir al-Muḥammadābādī narrated to us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Khālid ibn Qays and Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, both saying: Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "It is the prayer; among it is the even and among it is the odd." [143] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/239.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham narrated to us, saying: al-Dūraqī narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Murtafiʿ informed me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is [the day of] the last departure (al-nafr al-ākhir).

And al-Ḥasan informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Kathīr al-Qaysī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Abū Saʿīd ibn ʿAwf, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr say from the pulpit: "O assembly of pilgrims! You have come from near and far, upon the weak and the strong; you have kept your eyes awake, wearied your souls, and exhausted your bodies. Let none of you nullify his pilgrimage while he is unaware, by looking with his eye, or striking with his hand, or walking with his foot.

"O people of Mecca! Widen [your provision] for them as Allah has widened for you, and assist them in what they ask your help for, for they are the delegation of Allah and the pilgrims to the House of Allah, and they have a right over you. Ask me, for upon us the revelation was sent down, and we are the ones who have been entrusted with the interpretation (taʾwīl)." Then a man from the side of Zamzam stood and said: "A mouse entered my saddlebag while I was in the state of iḥrām." He said: "Kill the wicked rodent (fuwaysiqah)." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ and the ten nights." He said: "As for the even and the odd, it is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾; so these are the even and the odd. As for the ten nights, they are the eighth, ʿArafah, and the sacrifice." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage (yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar)." He said: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, and three days follow it."

Mujāhid, Masrūq and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the entire creation. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt: 49.]]: disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, land and sea, sun and moon, jinn and humankind. ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Allah, glorified is He, as He said: ﴿Say: He is Allah, One (Aḥad)﴾.

al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd: He intended by ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ the entire creation, of which there is a pair and an odd.

ʿAṭiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāt), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the evening prayer (ṣalāt al-maghrib). Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: it is number, of which there is an even and of which there is an odd. Muqātil: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is Adam and Eve, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. It was also said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Adam, whom Allah made even (shaffaʿahu) by his wife Eve.

Ibrāhīm and al-Qurẓī: the pair and the single. al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the two rakʿahs of the evening prayer, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the third rakʿah. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the House [the Kaʿbah]. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the levels of Paradise, since they are eight, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the levels of Hell, since they are seven; as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, swore by Paradise and Hell.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the days and nights, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection.

I heard Abū al-Qāsim ibn Ḥabīb say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ al-Shajarī say: I heard Abū Zayd Ḥātim ibn Maḥbūb al-Sāmī say: I heard ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār say: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say: "The odd (al-witr) is Allah, mighty and majestic, and He is also the even, by His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [[Sūrat al-Mujādilah: 7.]]." And I heard Abū al-Qāsim say: I heard Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Bakr al-Warrāq say: Abū Bakr was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "The even (shaf') is the opposition of the attributes of created beings: might and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and frailty, knowledge and ignorance, sight and blindness. The odd (witr) is the singularity of the attributes of Allah, glorified is He: might without humiliation, power without weakness, knowledge without ignorance, sight without blindness, and life without death, and what is similar to these."

It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Sacred Mosque of Mecca and the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Mosque of Jerusalem. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Qurʾān in the Ḥajj and the tamattuʿ in it, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the ifrād in it. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ is Muḥammad (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi), because through him the lights of faith burst forth and the darknesses of disbelief were dispelled.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ is the nights of Mūsā, by which he completed his appointment, by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We completed it with ten﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 142.]]. ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾: the created beings; ﴿Wal-Witr﴾: the Truth (al-Ḥaqq). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the obligatory duties (al-farāʾiḍ), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the voluntary practices (al-sunan). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the actions, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the intention, which is sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the act of worship that is repeated, such as prayer, fasting and zakāh, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the act of worship that is not repeated, such as Ḥajj. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the self (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ) when they are together, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the spirit without the self and the self without the spirit; as if Allah, glorified is He, swore by them in both states, of union and of separation. [[See the views on the meaning of shaf' and witr in the introduction of Fatḥ al-Bārī: 136.]]

The readers differed concerning ﴿al-Witr﴾. Yaḥyā [[Possibly: al-Jaʿdī.]] ibn Wathhāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the wāw, and this is the preference of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: "Because it is more common among the general public and more widespread. Moreover, when we examined the narrations that mention the witr of the prayer, we found them all in this dialect, and we have not heard in any of them the witr with a fatḥa. We also found that the meaning of witr in all of them, both in the prayer and in the sūrah, is one; and although they differ in their derivation, they are in origin one, and their interpretation is the single (fard), which is the opposite of the even (shaf')." The rest read it with a fatḥa on the wāw, and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and the preference of Abū Ḥātim. Both are well-attested dialects.

﴿Wal-Layli idhā yasri﴾ (and by the night when it passes). Most of the exegetes said: it means when it travels and departs. Qatādah said: when it comes and approaches.

Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and al-Kalbī said: it is the night of Muzdalifah.

The readers differed concerning His saying ﴿yasri﴾ (passes). The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā read it with a yāʾ in continuous recitation (waṣl); this is the preference of Abū Ḥātim and the transmission of Qutaybah, Naṣīr, and al-Sharyānī from al-Kisāʾī. Abū ʿUbayd said: al-Kisāʾī for a time used to say: "Affirm the yāʾ in continuous recitation and omit it when pausing, for the sake of the written script (al-kitāb)." Then he returned to omitting the yāʾ in both states, because it is the end of a verse (ra's āyah). This is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, and the preference of Abū ʿUbayd, following the orthography (lit. the script). Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb read the yāʾ in both states, according to the original form. Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: [the yāʾ] is dropped from it in agreement with the ends of verses.

Most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means "yasrī fīhi" (travels in it), as in their sayings: "a sleeping night" (layl nāʾim), "a fasting day" (nahār ṣāʾim), and "a concealing secret" (sirr kātim). al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs omit the yāʾ and make do with the kasra before it. Someone recited to me:

*Your palm is a palm that gives not a dirham in generosity, and another [palm] gives blood by the sword.*

And another said:

*My masters do not conceal the worth of a people, and perhaps my weariness will be lightened by my hardship.*

The historian said: I asked al-Akhfash about the reason for the omission of the yāʾ from *yasri*, and he said: "I will not answer you unless you spend a year sleeping at the door of my house." So I spent a year at the door of his house, then I asked him, and he said: "The night does not travel; rather, it is traveled in, and it is inflected (maṣrūf). When he inflected it, it lost its share of i'rāb (grammatical inflection). Do you not see His saying: ﴿And your mother was not unchaste (baghiyyan)﴾? [[Sūrat Maryam: 28.]]" He did not say *baghiyyah*, because he inflected it from *bāghiyah*.

﴿Hal fī dhālika qasamun﴾ (Is there in that an oath) — i.e., is there in what I have mentioned an oath sufficient and adequate (muqniʿ wa-mukfin) — ﴿li-dhī ḥijr﴾ (for one of intellect). He is called *dhū ḥijr* (possessor of restraint) because it restrains its possessor from what is not permitted and not becoming, just as it is called *ʿaql* (intellect) because it restrains (yaʿqiluhu) him from ugly deeds and disgraceful acts; and *nuhā* (restraint) because it forbids what is not fitting. The root of *ḥijr* is prevention. It is said of a man who is a master, dominant and in control of something: "He is indeed *dhū ḥijr*," and from this comes the saying: "The judge placed a *ḥajr* (interdiction) upon so-and-so."

**Makkī** (revealed in Mecca); it has 597 letters, 139 words, and 30 verses.

Widen [your provision] for them as Allah has widened for you, and assist them in what they ask your help for, for they are the delegation of Allah and the pilgrims to the House of Allah, and they have a right over you. Ask me, for upon us the revelation was sent down, and we are the ones who have been entrusted with the interpretation (taʾwīl)." Then a man from the side of Zamzam stood and said: "A mouse entered my saddlebag while I was in the state of iḥrām." He said: "Kill the wicked rodent (fuwaysiqah)." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ and the ten nights." He said: "As for the even and the odd, it is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾; so these are the even and the odd. As for the ten nights, they are the eighth, ʿArafah, and the sacrifice." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage (yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar)." He said: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, and three days follow it."

Mujāhid, Masrūq and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the entire creation. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt: 49.]]: disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, land and sea, sun and moon, jinn and humankind. ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Allah, glorified is He, as He said: ﴿Say: He is Allah, One (Aḥad)﴾.

al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd: He intended by ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ the entire creation, of which there is a pair and an odd.

ʿAṭiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāt), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the evening prayer (ṣalāt al-maghrib). Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: it is number, of which there is an even and of which there is an odd. Muqātil: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is Adam and Eve, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. It was also said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Adam, whom Allah made even (shaffaʿahu) by his wife Eve.

Ibrāhīm and al-Qurẓī: the pair and the single. al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the two rakʿahs of the evening prayer, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the third rakʿah. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the House [the Kaʿbah]. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the levels of Paradise, since they are eight, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the levels of Hell, since they are seven; as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, swore by Paradise and Hell.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the days and nights, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection.

I heard Abū al-Qāsim ibn Ḥabīb say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ al-Shajarī say: I heard Abū Zayd Ḥātim ibn Maḥbūb al-Sāmī say: I heard ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār say: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say: "The odd (al-witr) is Allah, mighty and majestic, and He is also the even, by His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [[Sūrat al-Mujādilah: 7.]]." And I heard Abū al-Qāsim say: I heard Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Bakr al-Warrāq say: Abū Bakr was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "The even (shaf') is the opposition of the attributes of created beings: might and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and frailty, knowledge and ignorance, sight and blindness. The odd (witr) is the singularity of the attributes of Allah, glorified is He: might without humiliation, power without weakness, knowledge without ignorance, sight without blindness, and life without death, and what is similar to these."

It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Sacred Mosque of Mecca and the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Mosque of Jerusalem. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Qurʾān in the Ḥajj and the tamattuʿ in it, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the ifrād in it. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ is Muḥammad (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi), because through him the lights of faith burst forth and the darknesses of disbelief were dispelled.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ is the nights of Mūsā, by which he completed his appointment, by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We completed it with ten﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 142.]]. ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾: the created beings; ﴿Wal-Witr﴾: the Truth (al-Ḥaqq). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the obligatory duties (al-farāʾiḍ), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the voluntary practices (al-sunan). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the actions, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the intention, which is sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the act of worship that is repeated, such as prayer, fasting and zakāh, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the act of worship that is not repeated, such as Ḥajj. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the self (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ) when they are together, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the spirit without the self and the self without the spirit; as if Allah, glorified is He, swore by them in both states, of union and of separation. [[See the views on the meaning of shaf' and witr in the introduction of Fatḥ al-Bārī: 136.]]

The readers differed concerning ﴿al-Witr﴾. Yaḥyā [[Possibly: al-Jaʿdī.]] ibn Wathhāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the wāw, and this is the preference of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: "Because it is more common among the general public and more widespread. Moreover, when we examined the narrations that mention the witr of the prayer, we found them all in this dialect, and we have not heard in any of them the witr with a fatḥa. We also found that the meaning of witr in all of them, both in the prayer and in the sūrah, is one; and although they differ in their derivation, they are in origin one, and their interpretation is the single (fard), which is the opposite of the even (shaf')." The rest read it with a fatḥa on the wāw, and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and the preference of Abū Ḥātim. Both are well-attested dialects.

﴿Wal-Layli idhā yasri﴾ (and by the night when it passes). Most of the exegetes said: it means when it travels and departs. Qatādah said: when it comes and approaches.

Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and al-Kalbī said: it is the night of Muzdalifah.

The readers differed concerning His saying ﴿yasri﴾ (passes). The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā read it with a yāʾ in continuous recitation (waṣl); this is the preference of Abū Ḥātim and the transmission of Qutaybah, Naṣīr, and al-Sharyānī from al-Kisāʾī. Abū ʿUbayd said: al-Kisāʾī for a time used to say: "Affirm the yāʾ in continuous recitation and omit it when pausing, for the sake of the written script (al-kitāb)." Then he returned to omitting the yāʾ in both states, because it is the end of a verse (ra's āyah). This is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, and the preference of Abū ʿUbayd, following the orthography (lit. the script). Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb read the yāʾ in both states, according to the original form. Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: [the yāʾ] is dropped from it in agreement with the ends of verses.

Most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means "yasrī fīhi" (travels in it), as in their sayings: "a sleeping night" (layl nāʾim), "a fasting day" (nahār ṣāʾim), and "a concealing secret" (sirr kātim). al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs omit the yāʾ and make do with the kasra before it. Someone recited to me:

*Your palm is a palm that gives not a dirham in generosity, and another [palm] gives blood by the sword.*

And another said:

*My masters do not conceal the worth of a people, and perhaps my weariness will be lightened by my hardship.*

The historian said: I asked al-Akhfash about the reason for the omission of the yāʾ from *yasri*, and he said: "I will not answer you unless you spend a year sleeping at the door of my house." So I spent a year at the door of his house, then I asked him, and he said: "The night does not travel; rather, it is traveled in, and it is inflected (maṣrūf). When he inflected it, it lost its share of i'rāb (grammatical inflection). Do you not see His saying: ﴿And your mother was not unchaste (baghiyyan)﴾? [[Sūrat Maryam: 28.]]" He did not say *baghiyyah*, because he inflected it from *bāghiyah*.

﴿Hal fī dhālika qasamun﴾ (Is there in that an oath) — i.e., is there in what I have mentioned an oath sufficient and adequate (muqniʿ wa-mukfin) — ﴿li-dhī ḥijr﴾ (for one of intellect). He is called *dhū ḥijr* (possessor of restraint) because it restrains its possessor from what is not permitted and not becoming, just as it is called *ʿaql* (intellect) because it restrains (yaʿqiluhu) him from ugly deeds and disgraceful acts; and *nuhā* (restraint) because it forbids what is not fitting. The root of *ḥijr* is prevention. It is said of a man who is a master, dominant and in control of something: "He is indeed *dhū ḥijr*," and from this comes the saying: "The judge placed a *ḥajr* (interdiction) upon so-and-so."

**Makkī** (revealed in Mecca); it has 597 letters, 139 words, and 30 verses.

Nāfil ibn Rāqim ibn Aḥmad al-Bābī informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Sādah narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the sūrah *Wal-Fajr* during the ten nights [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], he will be forgiven; and whoever recites it on the remaining days, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." [139] [[Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān: 10/341.]]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ (By the dawn). Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means the entire day. ʿAṭiyyah reported from him: the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). ʿUthmān ibn Muḥṣin reported from him: the dawn of Muharram. Qatādah said likewise: it is the first day of Muharram, from which the year bursts forth. Ḍaḥḥāk: the dawn of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, because Allah, glorified is He, joined the days to it. ʿIkrimah and Zayd ibn Aslam: the morning (al-ṣubḥ). Muqātil: it refers to the dawn of every year in its entirety. al-Qurẓī: the breaking of dawn from every day until the end of the world. In some tafsīrs: *al-Fajr* refers to the rocks and springs from which water bursts forth.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ (and ten nights). Mujāhid, Qatādah, Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and al-Ḥalabī said: they are the ten [nights] of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. ʿIkrimah: the nights of the Ḥajj. Masrūq said: they are the best days of the year. Abū Rawq, from Ḍaḥḥāk: they are the first ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, said: they are the last ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Yamān ibn Rabāb: the first ten [nights] of Muharram, of which the tenth is the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.

Akhbarani al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Ḥamdān narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Isḥāq al-Anṣārī narrated to us, saying: Manjāb ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmārah informed us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ḥassān narrated to us, from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, concerning His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾. He said: It is the dawn that you know. I said: ﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾? He said: The ten of al-Aḍḥā. I said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾? He said: its creation, as Allah says: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾. I said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾? He said: Allah is the Odd (witr). I said to him: Do you narrate this ḥadīth from any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. I said: From whom? He said: From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [140] [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 30/214; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 20/40.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Naṣrawayh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and ʿAbdah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, both saying: Abū al-Ḥusayn Zayd ibn al-Ḥubbāb al-ʿUklī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbās ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, saying: Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr wa Layālin ʿAshr﴾, said:

"[It is] the ten of sacrifice (al-naḥr); and the odd (witr) is the Day of ʿArafah; and the even (shaf') is the Day of Sacrifice." [141] [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/445.]]

And with the same chain, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Maslamah al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: Wāṣil ibn al-Sāʾib al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, saying: Abū Sawdah narrated to me, saying: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾. He said: "The even (shaf') is the Day of ʿArafah and the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and the odd (witr) is the night of sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr)." [142] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/238.]]

And Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Faḍl al-Fahandarī informed us, saying: Abū al-Ṭāhir al-Muḥammadābādī narrated to us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Khālid ibn Qays and Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, both saying: Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "It is the prayer; among it is the even and among it is the odd." [143] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/239.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham narrated to us, saying: al-Dūraqī narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Murtafiʿ informed me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is [the day of] the last departure (al-nafr al-ākhir).

And al-Ḥasan informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Kathīr al-Qaysī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Abū Saʿīd ibn ʿAwf, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr say from the pulpit: "O assembly of pilgrims! You have come from near and far, upon the weak and the strong; you have kept your eyes awake, wearied your souls, and exhausted your bodies. Let none of you nullify his pilgrimage while he is unaware, by looking with his eye, or striking with his hand, or walking with his foot.

"O people of Mecca! Widen [your provision] for them as Allah has widened for you, and assist them in what they ask your help for, for they are the delegation of Allah and the pilgrims to the House of Allah, and they have a right over you. Ask me, for upon us the revelation was sent down, and we are the ones who have been entrusted with the interpretation (taʾwīl)." Then a man from the side of Zamzam stood and said: "A mouse entered my saddlebag while I was in the state of iḥrām." He said: "Kill the wicked rodent (fuwaysiqah)." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ and the ten nights." He said: "As for the even and the odd, it is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾; so these are the even and the odd. As for the ten nights, they are the eighth, ʿArafah, and the sacrifice." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage (yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar)." He said: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, and three days follow it."

The readers differed concerning His saying ﴿yasri﴾ (passes). The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā read it with a yāʾ in continuous recitation (waṣl); this is the preference of Abū Ḥātim and the transmission of Qutaybah, Naṣīr, and al-Sharyānī from al-Kisāʾī. Abū ʿUbayd said: al-Kisāʾī for a time used to say: "Affirm the yāʾ in continuous recitation and omit it when pausing, for the sake of the written script (al-kitāb)." Then he returned to omitting the yāʾ in both states, because it is the end of a verse (ra's āyah). This is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, and the preference of Abū ʿUbayd, following the orthography (lit. the script). Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb read the yāʾ in both states, according to the original form. Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: [the yāʾ] is dropped from it in agreement with the ends of verses.

Most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means "yasrī fīhi" (travels in it), as in their sayings: "a sleeping night" (layl nāʾim), "a fasting day" (nahār ṣāʾim), and "a concealing secret" (sirr kātim). al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs omit the yāʾ and make do with the kasra before it. Someone recited to me:

*Your palm is a palm that gives not a dirham in generosity, and another [palm] gives blood by the sword.*

And another said:

*My masters do not conceal the worth of a people, and perhaps my weariness will be lightened by my hardship.*

The historian said: I asked al-Akhfash about the reason for the omission of the yāʾ from *yasri*, and he said: "I will not answer you unless you spend a year sleeping at the door of my house." So I spent a year at the door of his house, then I asked him, and he said: "The night does not travel; rather, it is traveled in, and it is inflected (maṣrūf). When he inflected it, it lost its share of i'rāb (grammatical inflection). Do you not see His saying: ﴿And your mother was not unchaste (baghiyyan)﴾? [[Sūrat Maryam: 28.]]" He did not say *baghiyyah*, because he inflected it from *bāghiyah*.

﴿Hal fī dhālika qasamun﴾ (Is there in that an oath) — i.e., is there in what I have mentioned an oath sufficient and adequate (muqniʿ wa-mukfin) — ﴿li-dhī ḥijr﴾ (for one of intellect). He is called *dhū ḥijr* (possessor of restraint) because it restrains its possessor from what is not permitted and not becoming, just as it is called *ʿaql* (intellect) because it restrains (yaʿqiluhu) him from ugly deeds and disgraceful acts; and *nuhā* (restraint) because it forbids what is not fitting. The root of *ḥijr* is prevention. It is said of a man who is a master, dominant and in control of something: "He is indeed *dhū ḥijr*," and from this comes the saying: "The judge placed a *ḥajr* (interdiction) upon so-and-so."

**Makkī** (revealed in Mecca); it has 597 letters, 139 words, and 30 verses.

Nāfil ibn Rāqim ibn Aḥmad al-Bābī informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Sādah narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the sūrah *Wal-Fajr* during the ten nights [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah], he will be forgiven; and whoever recites it on the remaining days, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." [139] [[Tafsīr Majmaʿ al-Bayān: 10/341.]]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.**

﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ (By the dawn). Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means the entire day. ʿAṭiyyah reported from him: the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-fajr). ʿUthmān ibn Muḥṣin reported from him: the dawn of Muharram. Qatādah said likewise: it is the first day of Muharram, from which the year bursts forth. Ḍaḥḥāk: the dawn of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, because Allah, glorified is He, joined the days to it. ʿIkrimah and Zayd ibn Aslam: the morning (al-ṣubḥ). Muqātil: it refers to the dawn of every year in its entirety. al-Qurẓī: the breaking of dawn from every day until the end of the world. In some tafsīrs: *al-Fajr* refers to the rocks and springs from which water bursts forth.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ (and ten nights). Mujāhid, Qatādah, Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Kalbī and al-Ḥalabī said: they are the ten [nights] of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. ʿIkrimah: the nights of the Ḥajj. Masrūq said: they are the best days of the year. Abū Rawq, from Ḍaḥḥāk: they are the first ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Abū Ẓabyān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, said: they are the last ten [nights] of Ramaḍān. Yamān ibn Rabāb: the first ten [nights] of Muharram, of which the tenth is the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ.

Akhbarani al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Ḥamdān narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Isḥāq al-Anṣārī narrated to us, saying: Manjāb ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmārah informed us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Ḥassān narrated to us, from ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī, concerning His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾. He said: It is the dawn that you know. I said: ﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾? He said: The ten of al-Aḍḥā. I said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾? He said: its creation, as Allah says: ﴿And We created you in pairs﴾. I said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾? He said: Allah is the Odd (witr). I said to him: Do you narrate this ḥadīth from any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)? He said: Yes. I said: From whom? He said: From Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet (ﷺ). [140] [[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī: 30/214; Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 20/40.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Naṣrawayh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and ʿAbdah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, both saying: Abū al-Ḥusayn Zayd ibn al-Ḥubbāb al-ʿUklī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbās ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, saying: Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr wa Layālin ʿAshr﴾, said:

"[It is] the ten of sacrifice (al-naḥr); and the odd (witr) is the Day of ʿArafah; and the even (shaf') is the Day of Sacrifice." [141] [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/445.]]

And with the same chain, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Maslamah al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: Wāṣil ibn al-Sāʾib al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, saying: Abū Sawdah narrated to me, saying: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾. He said: "The even (shaf') is the Day of ʿArafah and the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and the odd (witr) is the night of sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr)." [142] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/238.]]

And Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Faḍl al-Fahandarī informed us, saying: Abū al-Ṭāhir al-Muḥammadābādī narrated to us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Khālid ibn Qays and Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, both saying: Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "It is the prayer; among it is the even and among it is the odd." [143] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/239.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham narrated to us, saying: al-Dūraqī narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Murtafiʿ informed me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is [the day of] the last departure (al-nafr al-ākhir).

And al-Ḥasan informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Kathīr al-Qaysī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Abū Saʿīd ibn ʿAwf, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr say from the pulpit: "O assembly of pilgrims! You have come from near and far, upon the weak and the strong; you have kept your eyes awake, wearied your souls, and exhausted your bodies. Let none of you nullify his pilgrimage while he is unaware, by looking with his eye, or striking with his hand, or walking with his foot.

"O people of Mecca! Widen [your provision] for them as Allah has widened for you, and assist them in what they ask your help for, for they are the delegation of Allah and the pilgrims to the House of Allah, and they have a right over you. Ask me, for upon us the revelation was sent down, and we are the ones who have been entrusted with the interpretation (taʾwīl)." Then a man from the side of Zamzam stood and said: "A mouse entered my saddlebag while I was in the state of iḥrām." He said: "Kill the wicked rodent (fuwaysiqah)." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ and the ten nights." He said: "As for the even and the odd, it is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾; so these are the even and the odd. As for the ten nights, they are the eighth, ʿArafah, and the sacrifice." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage (yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar)." He said: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, and three days follow it."

Mujāhid, Masrūq and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the entire creation. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt: 49.]]: disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, land and sea, sun and moon, jinn and humankind. ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Allah, glorified is He, as He said: ﴿Say: He is Allah, One (Aḥad)﴾.

al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd: He intended by ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ the entire creation, of which there is a pair and an odd.

ʿAṭiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāt), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the evening prayer (ṣalāt al-maghrib). Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: it is number, of which there is an even and of which there is an odd. Muqātil: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is Adam and Eve, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. It was also said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Adam, whom Allah made even (shaffaʿahu) by his wife Eve.

Ibrāhīm and al-Qurẓī: the pair and the single. al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the two rakʿahs of the evening prayer, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the third rakʿah. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the House [the Kaʿbah]. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the levels of Paradise, since they are eight, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the levels of Hell, since they are seven; as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, swore by Paradise and Hell.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the days and nights, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection.

I heard Abū al-Qāsim ibn Ḥabīb say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ al-Shajarī say: I heard Abū Zayd Ḥātim ibn Maḥbūb al-Sāmī say: I heard ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār say: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say: "The odd (al-witr) is Allah, mighty and majestic, and He is also the even, by His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [[Sūrat al-Mujādilah: 7.]]." And I heard Abū al-Qāsim say: I heard Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Bakr al-Warrāq say: Abū Bakr was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "The even (shaf') is the opposition of the attributes of created beings: might and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and frailty, knowledge and ignorance, sight and blindness. The odd (witr) is the singularity of the attributes of Allah, glorified is He: might without humiliation, power without weakness, knowledge without ignorance, sight without blindness, and life without death, and what is similar to these."

It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Sacred Mosque of Mecca and the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Mosque of Jerusalem. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Qurʾān in the Ḥajj and the tamattuʿ in it, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the ifrād in it. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ is Muḥammad (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi), because through him the lights of faith burst forth and the darknesses of disbelief were dispelled.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ is the nights of Mūsā, by which he completed his appointment, by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We completed it with ten﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 142.]]. ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾: the created beings; ﴿Wal-Witr﴾: the Truth (al-Ḥaqq). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the obligatory duties (al-farāʾiḍ), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the voluntary practices (al-sunan). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the actions, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the intention, which is sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the act of worship that is repeated, such as prayer, fasting and zakāh, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the act of worship that is not repeated, such as Ḥajj. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the self (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ) when they are together, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the spirit without the self and the self without the spirit; as if Allah, glorified is He, swore by them in both states, of union and of separation. [[See the views on the meaning of shaf' and witr in the introduction of Fatḥ al-Bārī: 136.]]

The readers differed concerning ﴿al-Witr﴾. Yaḥyā [[Possibly: al-Jaʿdī.]] ibn Wathhāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the wāw, and this is the preference of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: "Because it is more common among the general public and more widespread. Moreover, when we examined the narrations that mention the witr of the prayer, we found them all in this dialect, and we have not heard in any of them the witr with a fatḥa. We also found that the meaning of witr in all of them, both in the prayer and in the sūrah, is one; and although they differ in their derivation, they are in origin one, and their interpretation is the single (fard), which is the opposite of the even (shaf')." The rest read it with a fatḥa on the wāw, and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and the preference of Abū Ḥātim. Both are well-attested dialects.

﴿Wal-Layli idhā yasri﴾ (and by the night when it passes). Most of the exegetes said: it means when it travels and departs. Qatādah said: when it comes and approaches.

Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and al-Kalbī said: it is the night of Muzdalifah.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Naṣrawayh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān and ʿAbdah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, both saying: Abū al-Ḥusayn Zayd ibn al-Ḥubbāb al-ʿUklī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbās ibn ʿUqbah narrated to us, saying: Ḥusayn ibn Nuʿaym al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to me, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Wal-Fajr wa Layālin ʿAshr﴾, said:

"[It is] the ten of sacrifice (al-naḥr); and the odd (witr) is the Day of ʿArafah; and the even (shaf') is the Day of Sacrifice." [141] [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/445.]]

And with the same chain, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Yūsuf ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd ibn Maslamah al-Umawī narrated to us, saying: Wāṣil ibn al-Sāʾib al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, saying: Abū Sawdah narrated to me, saying: Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾. He said: "The even (shaf') is the Day of ʿArafah and the Day of al-Aḍḥā, and the odd (witr) is the night of sacrifice (laylat al-naḥr)." [142] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/238.]]

And Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Faḍl al-Fahandarī informed us, saying: Abū al-Ṭāhir al-Muḥammadābādī narrated to us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying: Khālid ibn Qays and Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, both saying: Qatādah narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn ʿĀṣim, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "It is the prayer; among it is the even and among it is the odd." [143] [[Zād al-Masīr li-Ibn al-Jawzī: 8/239.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Lu'lu' narrated to us, saying: al-Haytham narrated to us, saying: al-Dūraqī narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Muḥammad ibn al-Murtafiʿ informed me that he heard Ibn al-Zubayr say: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is [the day of] the last departure (al-nafr al-ākhir).

And al-Ḥasan informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Kathīr al-Qaysī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, from Abū Saʿīd ibn ʿAwf, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr say from the pulpit: "O assembly of pilgrims! You have come from near and far, upon the weak and the strong; you have kept your eyes awake, wearied your souls, and exhausted your bodies. Let none of you nullify his pilgrimage while he is unaware, by looking with his eye, or striking with his hand, or walking with his foot.

"O people of Mecca! Widen [your provision] for them as Allah has widened for you, and assist them in what they ask your help for, for they are the delegation of Allah and the pilgrims to the House of Allah, and they have a right over you. Ask me, for upon us the revelation was sent down, and we are the ones who have been entrusted with the interpretation (taʾwīl)." Then a man from the side of Zamzam stood and said: "A mouse entered my saddlebag while I was in the state of iḥrām." He said: "Kill the wicked rodent (fuwaysiqah)." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ and the ten nights." He said: "As for the even and the odd, it is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾; so these are the even and the odd. As for the ten nights, they are the eighth, ʿArafah, and the sacrifice." Another man stood and said: "Inform us about the Day of the Greatest Pilgrimage (yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar)." He said: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, and three days follow it."

Mujāhid, Masrūq and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the entire creation. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [[Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt: 49.]]: disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, land and sea, sun and moon, jinn and humankind. ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Allah, glorified is He, as He said: ﴿Say: He is Allah, One (Aḥad)﴾.

al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd: He intended by ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾ the entire creation, of which there is a pair and an odd.

ʿAṭiyyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāt), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the evening prayer (ṣalāt al-maghrib). Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: it is number, of which there is an even and of which there is an odd. Muqātil: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is Adam and Eve, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Lord, blessed and exalted is He. It was also said: ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is Adam, whom Allah made even (shaffaʿahu) by his wife Eve.

Ibrāhīm and al-Qurẓī: the pair and the single. al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the two rakʿahs of the evening prayer, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the third rakʿah. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the House [the Kaʿbah]. al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the levels of Paradise, since they are eight, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the levels of Hell, since they are seven; as if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, swore by Paradise and Hell.

Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the days and nights, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the day after which there is no night, which is the Day of Resurrection.

I heard Abū al-Qāsim ibn Ḥabīb say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ al-Shajarī say: I heard Abū Zayd Ḥātim ibn Maḥbūb al-Sāmī say: I heard ʿAbd al-Jabbār ibn al-ʿAlāʾ al-ʿAṭṭār say: I heard Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah say: "The odd (al-witr) is Allah, mighty and majestic, and He is also the even, by His saying: ﴿There is no secret conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them﴾ [[Sūrat al-Mujādilah: 7.]]." And I heard Abū al-Qāsim say: I heard Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: I heard Abū ʿAbd Allah ibn Abī Bakr al-Warrāq say: Abū Bakr was asked about ﴿Wash-Shaf'i wal-Witr﴾, and he said: "The even (shaf') is the opposition of the attributes of created beings: might and humiliation, power and weakness, strength and frailty, knowledge and ignorance, sight and blindness. The odd (witr) is the singularity of the attributes of Allah, glorified is He: might without humiliation, power without weakness, knowledge without ignorance, sight without blindness, and life without death, and what is similar to these."

It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Sacred Mosque of Mecca and the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the Mosque of Jerusalem. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the Qurʾān in the Ḥajj and the tamattuʿ in it, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the ifrād in it. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: ﴿Wal-Fajr﴾ is Muḥammad (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi), because through him the lights of faith burst forth and the darknesses of disbelief were dispelled.

﴿Wa-Layālin ʿAshr﴾ is the nights of Mūsā, by which he completed his appointment, by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And We completed it with ten﴾ [[Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 142.]]. ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾: the created beings; ﴿Wal-Witr﴾: the Truth (al-Ḥaqq). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the obligatory duties (al-farāʾiḍ), and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the voluntary practices (al-sunan). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the actions, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the intention, which is sincerity (al-ikhlāṣ). It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the act of worship that is repeated, such as prayer, fasting and zakāh, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the act of worship that is not repeated, such as Ḥajj. It was also said: ﴿Wash-Shaf'i﴾ is the self (nafs) and the spirit (rūḥ) when they are together, and ﴿Wal-Witr﴾ is the spirit without the self and the self without the spirit; as if Allah, glorified is He, swore by them in both states, of union and of separation. [[See the views on the meaning of shaf' and witr in the introduction of Fatḥ al-Bārī: 136.]]

The readers differed concerning ﴿al-Witr﴾. Yaḥyā [[Possibly: al-Jaʿdī.]] ibn Wathhāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the wāw, and this is the preference of Abū ʿUbayd. He said: "Because it is more common among the general public and more widespread. Moreover, when we examined the narrations that mention the witr of the prayer, we found them all in this dialect, and we have not heard in any of them the witr with a fatḥa. We also found that the meaning of witr in all of them, both in the prayer and in the sūrah, is one; and although they differ in their derivation, they are in origin one, and their interpretation is the single (fard), which is the opposite of the even (shaf')." The rest read it with a fatḥa on the wāw, and this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz and the preference of Abū Ḥātim. Both are well-attested dialects.

﴿Wal-Layli idhā yasri﴾ (and by the night when it passes). Most of the exegetes said: it means when it travels and departs. Qatādah said: when it comes and approaches.

Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and al-Kalbī said: it is the night of Muzdalifah.

The readers differed concerning His saying ﴿yasri﴾ (passes). The people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĪsā read it with a yāʾ in continuous recitation (waṣl); this is the preference of Abū Ḥātim and the transmission of Qutaybah, Naṣīr, and al-Sharyānī from al-Kisāʾī. Abū ʿUbayd said: al-Kisāʾī for a time used to say: "Affirm the yāʾ in continuous recitation and omit it when pausing, for the sake of the written script (al-kitāb)." Then he returned to omitting the yāʾ in both states, because it is the end of a verse (ra's āyah). This is the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim, and the preference of Abū ʿUbayd, following the orthography (lit. the script). Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb read the yāʾ in both states, according to the original form. Al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad said: [the yāʾ] is dropped from it in agreement with the ends of verses.

Most of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: it means "yasrī fīhi" (travels in it), as in their sayings: "a sleeping night" (layl nāʾim), "a fasting day" (nahār ṣāʾim), and "a concealing secret" (sirr kātim). al-Farrāʾ said: the Arabs omit the yāʾ and make do with the kasra before it. Someone recited to me:

*Your palm is a palm that gives not a dirham in generosity, and another [palm] gives blood by the sword.*

And another said:

*My masters do not conceal the worth of a people, and perhaps my weariness will be lightened by my hardship.*

The historian said: I asked al-Akhfash about the reason for the omission of the yāʾ from *yasri*, and he said: "I will not answer you unless you spend a year sleeping at the door of my house." So I spent a year at the door of his house, then I asked him, and he said: "The night does not travel; rather, it is traveled in, and it is inflected (maṣrūf). When he inflected it, it lost its share of i'rāb (grammatical inflection). Do you not see His saying: ﴿And your mother was not unchaste (baghiyyan)﴾? [[Sūrat Maryam: 28.]]" He did not say *baghiyyah*, because he inflected it from *bāghiyah*.

﴿Hal fī dhālika qasamun﴾ (Is there in that an oath) — i.e., is there in what I have mentioned an oath sufficient and adequate (muqniʿ wa-mukfin) — ﴿li-dhī ḥijr﴾ (for one of intellect). He is called *dhū ḥijr* (possessor of restraint) because it restrains its possessor from what is not permitted and not becoming, just as it is called *ʿaql* (intellect) because it restrains (yaʿqiluhu) him from ugly deeds and disgraceful acts; and *nuhā* (restraint) because it forbids what is not fitting. The root of *ḥijr* is prevention. It is said of a man who is a master, dominant and in control of something: "He is indeed *dhū ḥijr*," and from this comes the saying: "The judge placed a *ḥajr* (interdiction) upon so-and-so."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 6–14:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram,﴾. The common readers recited it with tanwin (ʿĀdin, Iraman). Al-Hasan recited (bi-ʿĀdi Iram) as an idafa (construct). The common readers recited (Iram) with a kasra on the alif, while Mujahid recited it with a fatha. The historian said: whoever recites it with a fatha on the alif likens them to the ārām (landmarks), whose singular is ārim.

The scholars differed over the meaning of His words ﴿Iram﴾. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa al-Baqirhi related to us, saying: Ibn ʿAlawiyya related to us, saying: Ismaʿil related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from someone who told him that Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab used to say: ﴿Iram of the pillars, Damascus﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan related to us, saying: Ibn Marwan related to us, saying: ʿAli ibn Harb al-Tai related to us, saying: Abu al-Ashhab Hud related to us from ʿAwf al-Aʿrabi, from Khalid al-Rabʿi, regarding ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾, that he said: Damascus. Ikrima and Abu Saʿid al-Maqburi also said this.

Al-Qurazi said: it is Alexandria. Mujahid said: it is Irama, meaning "the ancient." Qatada said: they are a tribe of ʿAd. Abu Ishaq said: it is the grandfather of ʿAd, namely ʿAd ibn ʿAwis ibn Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh.

Muqatil said: Iram is a tribe from the people of ʿAd in which kingship resided, and they were the place of Mahra. ʿAd was their father, so they were attributed to him. He is Iram ibn ʿAd ibn Shamr ibn Sam ibn Nuh.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Tayyib al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAli related to us, saying: Fadl ibn Khalid informed us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim that he used to recite ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ with a fatha on the alif and the ra', and that Iram means destruction. He said: "Arama banu fulan," meaning they were destroyed. This is also the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

It is also narrated from al-Dahhak that he recited ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾, meaning: He destroyed them and made them crumbled bones (rumim). The correct view is that it is the name of a tribe or a town, and therefore it is not inflected (with kasra).[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/220.]]

As for His words ﴿of the pillars﴾, a group said: it means possessors of height, strength and might.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Abu Hatim related to us, saying: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, related to us, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih related to me from one who related to him, from al-Miqdam, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he mentioned ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ and said: "A man among them would come with a rock, carry it on his shoulder, and throw it upon whatever tribe he wished, destroying them."[144][[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/347; Fath al-Bari: 8/538.]]

Al-Kalbi said: the height of a man among them was four hundred cubits. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means their height was like pillars, and the Arabs call a tall man "muʿammad." Muqatil said: the height of one of them was twelve cubits. Others said: they were only called "of the pillars" because they were people of mobile pillars (tents), who followed the rain and moved to pasture wherever it was, and then returned to their dwellings and did not stay in one place.

Al-Kalbi said: Iram is the one to whom the lineage of ʿAd, Thamud, the people of the Sawad and the people of al-Jazira converge. It used to be said: "ʿAd Iram and Thamud Iram." Then God destroyed ʿAd, then Thamud, and the people of the Sawad and al-Jazira remained. They were people of pillars, tents and livestock in spring, and when the grass withered they returned to their dwellings; they were people of gardens and crops, and their dwellings were in Wadi al-Qura, which is the one of which God says: ﴿the like of which was not created in the lands﴾.

It was also said: they were named "of the pillars" because of a building one of them built, whose pillars he reinforced and whose structure he raised. ʿImad, ʿumud and ʿumud are plurals of ʿamud (pillar).

What Abu al-Qasim the exegete informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbdullah Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Abu Jaʿfar Ahmad ibn Mahdi ibn Rustam al-Isfahani informed us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih al-Misri related to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿa related to me. And Abu al-Qasim informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbdus al-Taraʾifi informed us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid al-Darji informed us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿa related to me from Khalid ibn Abi ʿImran, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from ʿAbdullah ibn Qilaba, that he went out seeking camels of his that had strayed. While he was in the deserts of Aden, he came upon a city in those wastelands, with a fortress upon which were great palaces and tall pillars. When he drew near, he thought there was someone there he could ask about his camels, but he saw no one going out or coming in. He dismounted, tethered his mount, drew his sword and entered through the gate of the fortress. When he entered the fortress, he found two enormous gates, larger than any he had seen, both inlaid with white and red rubies. When he saw this he was astonished and amazed, and he opened one of the gates, and there was a city the like of which no one had seen. Each palace had pillars of chrysolite and ruby hanging beneath it, and above each palace were upper chambers:

[Take heed, O you deceived by a long life... I am Shaddad ibn ʿAd, owner of the lofty fortress,
and brother of might and hardship and the gathered kingdom... the abode of the people of the earth fears my threat and warning,
and I ruled East and West with a mighty authority... and by the bounty of kingship, its troops and its multitude,
Then Hud came, and we were in error before Hud... he called us, had we accepted him, to the right course,
but we disobeyed him and cried out, "Is there any escape?" Then a cry came upon us, descending from the distant horizon,
so we were gathered like crops cut down in a wide wilderness.]

﴿And Thamud﴾, that is, and Thamud, ﴿who hewed﴾, meaning carved and cut out, ﴿the rock﴾, the stones, singular "sakhra," ﴿in the valley﴾, meaning the valley of the Qura. They carved houses from them, as God says: ﴿and they used to hew houses out of the mountains, secure﴾.[[Surat al-Hijr: 82.]]

The people of biographical history said: the first to carve mountains, rocks and marble were Thamud. They built from houses and dwellings two thousand and seven hundred thousand, all of stone. Abu Jaʿfar, Abu Hatim and Warsh pronounced the ya' in "al-wad" when pausing and continuing, Ibn Kathir in the narration of al-Bazzi and al-ʿAwwas and Yaʿqub kept it according to the original, while the others omitted it in both situations because it is the end of a verse.

﴿And Pharaoh, possessor of stakes﴾. They differed concerning it. Some said: it means possessor of hosts and armies who strengthened his command and secured his kingdom, and the soldiers were called "stakes" because of the many tents they pitched and fixed on their journeys. This is the narration of ʿAtiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Qatada said: he was called "possessor of stakes" because he had canopies, playgrounds and stakes to which he was tied, and they played beneath them. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: it means possessor of firm construction. Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: he had minarets on which he tortured people. Mujahid and others said: he tortured people with stakes; when he became angry with someone he would stretch him on the ground and stake his hands, feet and head to the ground.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Mukhallad related to us, saying: Ibn ʿAlawiyya related to us, saying: Ismaʿil related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us from Ibn Sam'an, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, that when Pharaoh was told "possessor of stakes," [it was] that she was a woman, namely the woman of his treasurer Kharbil,[[Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (15/306) cited from al-Tha'labi that his name was Hizqil.]] son of Nuhabil, and he was a believer who concealed his faith for a hundred years,[[As mentioned in Taj al-Arus (7/302); it was also said six hundred years, mentioned by al-Jaza'iri in al-Qisas: 253.]] and he had met some of the companions of Joseph; and his wife was the hairdresser of Pharaoh's daughter. One day, while she was combing the head of Pharaoh's daughter, the comb fell from her hand, and she said: "Woe to the one who disbelieves in God." Pharaoh's daughter said: "Do you have a god other than my father?" She said: "My God and your father's God and the God of the heavens and the earth is one, without partner."

She got up, entered upon her father weeping. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "The hairdresser, the woman of your treasurer, claims that your god and her god and the god of the heavens and the earth is one, without partner." He sent for her and asked her about that, and she said: "You have spoken the truth." He said to her: "Woe to you! Disbelieve in your god and affirm that I am your god." She said: "I will not do that." So he stretched her between four stakes, then sent upon her snakes and scorpions, and said to her: "Disbelieve in God, or I will torture you with this torment for two months." She said: "By God, if you tortured me for seventy months I would not disbelieve in God, the Exalted."

He said: She had two daughters, so he brought the elder daughter and slaughtered her in front of her mouth, and said to her: "Disbelieve in God, or I will slaughter your younger daughter in front of your mouth." The younger was a nursing infant, and she felt a great pang for her. She said: "Even if you slaughtered whoever is on the earth in front of my mouth, I would not disbelieve in God, the Exalted."

He said: He brought the daughter, and when she was brought forward, laid down upon her chest and they were about to slaughter her, the mother became distressed. God loosened the tongue of her daughter, and she spoke, for she was one of the four who spoke while infants. She said: "O mother, do not be distressed, for God has built for you a house in Paradise. Be patient, for you are going to the mercy and honor of God." He said: She was slaughtered, and she had not lingered before she died, and God settled her in Paradise.

He said: He sent to seek her husband Kharbil, but they could not find him. It was said to Pharaoh: "He has been seen in such and such a place, in such and such mountains." He sent two men in pursuit of him, and they reached him while he was praying, and three rows of wild beasts were behind him praying. When they saw that, they turned back. Kharbil said: "O God, You know that I concealed my faith for a hundred years, and no one discovered me. Of these two men, whichever concealed [my whereabouts] from me, guide him to Your religion and give him from the world what he asks; and of these two men, whichever revealed me, hasten his punishment in this world, and make his final destination the Fire." The two men returned to Pharaoh. One of them took heed and believed, while the other informed Pharaoh of the story before the chiefs. Pharaoh said to him: "Was there anyone with you other than yourself?" He said: "Yes."

He said: "And who was with you?" He said: "So-and-so." He summoned him. He said: "Is what this one says true?" He said: "No, I did not see anything of what he said." Pharaoh gave him and rewarded him generously. As for the other, he killed him and then crucified him.

He said: Pharaoh had married a woman, one of the most beautiful women of the Children of Israel, called Asiya daughter of Muzahim. When she saw what Pharaoh had done to the hairdresser, she said: "How could I bear to be patient with what Pharaoh has done, while I am a Muslim and he is a disbeliever?" While she was thus deliberating within herself, Pharaoh entered upon her and sat near her. She said: "O Pharaoh, you are the worst and most vile of creatures. You went to the hairdresser and killed her." He said: "Perhaps the madness that afflicted her has also afflicted you."

She said: "I have no madness. My God and your God and the God of the heavens and the earth is one, without partner." He tore at her and beat her, and sent for her parents, summoned them, and told them the matter, that the madness which had afflicted the hairdresser had afflicted her. She said: "I seek refuge in God from that. I testify that my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of the heavens and the earth is one, without partner." Her father said: "O Asiya, are you not the best of the women of the Amalekites, and your husband the god of the Amalekites?" She said: "I seek refuge in God from that, if what you say is true. So tell him: let him crown me with a crown, with the sun in front of it, the moon behind it, and the stars around it." Pharaoh said to them: "Get out of my presence." He stretched her between four stakes to torture her. God opened for her a gate to Paradise to make easier for her what Pharaoh did to her. At that moment she said: ﴿My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾, meaning from Pharaoh's intercourse, ﴿and save me from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning from Pharaoh and his party. God took her soul and settled her in Paradise.[[The story with variations in the long narrations of al-Tabarani: 115; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/420.]]

It was also said: the stakes are a metaphor for the stability of his kingdom, the length of his reign and the severity of his majesty, like the firmness of stakes in the earth, as the poet al-Aswad said:

﴿In the shade of a king of firm stakes﴾.[[Maʿani al-Qur'an by al-Nahhas: 6/85; Muʿjam al-Buldan: 1/272, whose opening line is: "And they indeed delighted therein in the finest living."]]

﴿Who transgressed in the lands and multiplied corruption therein, so your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.﴾ Qatada said: it means a kind of punishment He poured upon them. Al-Suddi said: every day a different kind of punishment. It was also said: the pain of punishment. The people of the meanings said: this is figurative, because the whip, in their view, is the extreme of punishment, so it applies to every punishment. The poet said:

﴿Do you not see that God has made His religion manifest, and poured upon the disbelievers a whip of punishment?﴾

﴿Indeed your Lord is in the watchtower.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: He, glory be to Him, sees and hears. Muqatil said: He watches over people on the Sirat (bridge), so He placed a watch of angels with them, carrying hooks, staves and thorns. Al-Dahhak said: in a watchtower over the people of wrongdoing and disobedience. It was also said: its meaning is that the return of creation and their destination is to His judgment and command. Al-Hasan and ʿIkrima said: He watches the deeds of the children of Adam. Also from Muqatil: their passing by it. ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah: no one escapes Him. Yaman: there is no escape from Him. Al-Suddi: He sets the Fire on their paths until it destroys them. The word "al-mirsad" and "al-marsad" mean the path, and the plural of "al-mirsad" is "marasid," and the plural of "al-marsad" is "marasid."

Muqsim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Over Hell there are seven checkpoints. The servants are questioned at the first of them about the testimony that there is no god but God. If he brings it complete, he passes to the second, where he is asked about prayer. If he brings it complete, he passes to the third, where he is asked about zakat. If he brings it complete, he passes to the fourth, where he is asked about fasting. If he brings it complete, he passes to the fifth, where he is asked about Hajj. If he brings it complete, he passes to the sixth, where he is asked about 'Umra. If he brings it complete, he passes to the seventh, where he is asked about wrongful acts. If he is clear of them, well; otherwise it is said, "Wait and see." If he has voluntary acts, they complete his deeds, and when he has finished with them he is taken to Paradise.

As for His words ﴿of the pillars﴾, a group said: it means possessors of height, strength and might.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash related to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Abu Hatim related to us, saying: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, related to us, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih related to me from one who related to him, from al-Miqdam, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he mentioned ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ and said: "A man among them would come with a rock, carry it on his shoulder, and throw it upon whatever tribe he wished, destroying them."[144][[Tafsir al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/347; Fath al-Bari: 8/538.]]

Al-Kalbi said: the height of a man among them was four hundred cubits. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means their height was like pillars, and the Arabs call a tall man "muʿammad." Muqatil said: the height of one of them was twelve cubits. Others said: they were only called "of the pillars" because they were people of mobile pillars (tents), who followed the rain and moved to pasture wherever it was, and then returned to their dwellings and did not stay in one place.

Al-Kalbi said: Iram is the one to whom the lineage of ʿAd, Thamud, the people of the Sawad and the people of al-Jazira converge. It used to be said: "ʿAd Iram and Thamud Iram." Then God destroyed ʿAd, then Thamud, and the people of the Sawad and al-Jazira remained. They were people of pillars, tents and livestock in spring, and when the grass withered they returned to their dwellings; they were people of gardens and crops, and their dwellings were in Wadi al-Qura, which is the one of which God says: ﴿the like of which was not created in the lands﴾.

It was also said: they were named "of the pillars" because of a building one of them built, whose pillars he reinforced and whose structure he raised. ʿImad, ʿumud and ʿumud are plurals of ʿamud (pillar).

And Abu al-Qasim informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbdus al-Taraʾifi informed us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Saʿid al-Darji informed us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿa related to me from Khalid ibn Abi ʿImran, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from ʿAbdullah ibn Qilaba, that he went out seeking camels of his that had strayed. While he was in the deserts of Aden, he came upon a city in those wastelands, with a fortress upon which were great palaces and tall pillars. When he drew near, he thought there was someone there he could ask about his camels, but he saw no one going out or coming in. He dismounted, tethered his mount, drew his sword and entered through the gate of the fortress. When he entered the fortress, he found two enormous gates, larger than any he had seen, both inlaid with white and red rubies. When he saw this he was astonished and amazed, and he opened one of the gates, and there was a city the like of which no one had seen. Each palace had pillars of chrysolite and ruby hanging beneath it, and above each palace were upper chambers:

[Take heed, O you deceived by a long life... I am Shaddad ibn ʿAd, owner of the lofty fortress,
and brother of might and hardship and the gathered kingdom... the abode of the people of the earth fears my threat and warning,
and I ruled East and West with a mighty authority... and by the bounty of kingship, its troops and its multitude,
Then Hud came, and we were in error before Hud... he called us, had we accepted him, to the right course,
but we disobeyed him and cried out, "Is there any escape?" Then a cry came upon us, descending from the distant horizon,
so we were gathered like crops cut down in a wide wilderness.]

﴿And Thamud﴾, that is, and Thamud, ﴿who hewed﴾, meaning carved and cut out, ﴿the rock﴾, the stones, singular "sakhra," ﴿in the valley﴾, meaning the valley of the Qura. They carved houses from them, as God says: ﴿and they used to hew houses out of the mountains, secure﴾.[[Surat al-Hijr: 82.]]
