'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari', who said: Hilal told me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hana'i, who said: in the recitation of Ubayy: *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-āminatu al-muṭma'innah* (O soul, secure and at rest).

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi informed me, saying: my father told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj told us, saying: Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*: he said: the one content with Allah's decree, who knows that what befell her would not have missed her, and that what missed her would not have befallen her. Ibn Kaysan said: the sincere one. Ibn 'Ata': she is the one who knows Allah, glory be to Him, and does not turn away from Him for the blink of an eye. It was also said: the one at rest through the remembrance of Allah. Its explanation is: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah﴾. It was also said: she is the one who trusts in Allah, exalted is He, and is confident in what He has guaranteed her of provision.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/57.]]

﴿Return to your Lord﴾. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse and the time of this saying. Some people said: it is said to her at death: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-'Askari told us, saying: al-'Ataridi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Return to your Lord, content and pleasing﴾: he said: this is at her departure from the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: ﴿Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Furati told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah told us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sulaymani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: When the believing servant dies, Allah, glory be to Him, sends two angels, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. It is said to her: "Come out, O soul at rest, come out to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is well pleased with you." She comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone ever smelled, and the angels are on the edges of the heaven.

They say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, a good breath." No gate is passed except that it is opened for her, and no angel except that he prays for her, until she is brought before the Merciful. Then the angels prostrate, and they say: "Our Lord, this is Your servant so-and-so, who used to worship You and never associated anything with You." He says: "Tell him to prostrate," and the soul prostrates. Then Mikail is called, and He says: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers until I ask you about her on the Day of Resurrection." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants grow for him in it. If he had any Qur'an with him, its light suffices him; if he did not, a likeness of the sun is made for him in his grave, and he is like a bride who sleeps, and no one wakes her except the dearest of her family to her, so she rises from her sleep as if she had not had enough of it. When the disbeliever dies, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends two angels and sends with them a piece of the most foul and rough cloth of every rough thing, and it is said: "O wicked soul, come out to scalding water and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: al-Masuhi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' al-Hanafi told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A man recited before the Prophet (ﷺ), *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*. Abu Bakr said: "How beautiful this is!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the angel will say it to you [at death]."[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/485, no. 35591; what is between brackets is from it.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Qasri informed us there, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari informed me. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Salim told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Munay' told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came, which was not seen in its form, and entered his bier, and then it was not seen leaving it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and the one reciting it was not seen: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, content and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.﴾

Others said: it is only said to her at the Resurrection: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, to your companion, your body. So Allah, glory be to Him, commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This view was held by 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and it is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as *fa-dkhulī fī 'abdī* ("enter among My servant"), with the monotheistic reading.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, those like you among the righteous servants of your Lord.

Some people of spiritual allusion said: ﴿O soul at rest﴾ in the world, ﴿return to Allah﴾ by leaving it; and returning to Allah is following the path of the Hereafter. ﴿Content﴾ with Allah in what He has prepared for her, ﴿pleasing﴾ to her Lord, who is pleased with her. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Some said: that is, with My servants, ﴿My Paradise﴾; the meaning of the verse involves inversion and reordering, and this was the view of Muqatil, al-Qurazi and Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And enter, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾, that is, with Our prophets in Paradise. Al-Akhfash said: that is, among My party. And another said: it is the command for the spirits to return to their bodies. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyyah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, regarding this verse, ﴿O soul at rest﴾, he said: it is the soul of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib; it was revealed concerning him on the day he was martyred at Uhud. Rather, his soul descended in the presence of the Lord of the worlds, honored and exalted above those near Him, until Allah, glory be to Him, returns it to Hamzah in tranquility, calm, and honor.

It was also revealed concerning Habib ibn 'Adi, whom the people of Makkah crucified and turned his face toward Madinah. He said: "O Allah, if I have any good with You, turn my face toward Your qibla." So Allah, glory be to Him, turned his face toward the qibla without anyone turning it, and no one could turn it. Its ruling is general for all believers who are at rest.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 15–30**

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and abundance﴾: that is, He tries him with blessing and plenty. ﴿He honors him with wealth and bestows on him favors through what He has widened for him, so he says: "My Lord has honored me,"﴾ and so he rejoices, is glad, praises Him for it and gives thanks. ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, measuring it out and straitening his sustenance, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me,"﴾ that is, has disgraced me with poverty. He does not thank Allah for what He has given him of soundness of limbs and the health and well-being He has provided. Qatadah said: "How quickly the son of Adam becomes ungrateful!"

The recitation of the majority is ﴿fa-qadara﴾ with a light *dal*. Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a doubled *dal* (*faqqadara*). Both are dialectal variants. Abu 'Amr used to say: *qadara* means *qattara* (to restrict), and *qaddara* means to give him what suffices him. Had it been the latter, he would not have said, "My Lord has humiliated me." Then He responded to him, saying: ﴿No!﴾ I did not test him with wealth because of his honor with Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his lowliness with Me. Poverty and wealth are part of My decree and My judgment. So I do not honor the one to whom I have given wealth and abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate the one whom I have humbled with poverty and scarcity of the world. Rather, I honor the one who honors Me by obedience, and I humiliate the one who humbles himself by disobedience to Me. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *kalla* (no) is that it is not fitting for him to be this way; rather, it is fitting that he praise Him for both circumstances, wealth and poverty.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honor the orphan﴾, meaning: I humiliated the one I humiliated because he does not honor the orphan.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The people of Basra read *yukrimūna* and what follows it entirely with the *yā'* (third person), while the others read it with the *tā'* (second person). ﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾: Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa read *tahāḍḍūna* with an *alif* and an open *tā'*. Al-Shadhhari related from al-Kisa'i *tuḥāḍḍūna* with a *ḍammah* on the *tā'*. Others read *taḥuḍḍūna* without the *alif*. ﴿And you devour the inheritance greedily﴾: *al-turāth* is the inheritance, and *aklan lamman* means intense, excessive eating. Al-Hasan said: he eats his own share and the share of others. Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *al-lamm* is transgression in inheritance; he consumes his own inheritance and that of others. Ibn Zayd said: *al-akl al-lamm* is the eating of one who devours everything he finds without asking whether it is lawful or unlawful, consuming what is his and what belongs to others. This was because they did not give inheritance to women or children. [The verse] ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾ and so on was recited. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, *lammtu mā 'alā al-khiwān* (I licked up what was on the tray), when one reaches what is on it and eats it all together.

﴿And you love wealth with an abundant love﴾: *jamman* means much, abundant. It is said *jamma al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ* (the water gathered in the basin) when it became abundant and collected. ﴿No!﴾ This is not how the matter ought to be. Then He informed about those who lament over what they have passed by, when it will no longer benefit them, saying, exalted is He who speaks:

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder﴾: meaning, repeatedly, time after time, so that everything upon it is crushed.

﴿And your Lord comes﴾: al-Hasan said: His command and His judgment. The people of spiritual allusion (*ahl al-ishārah*) said: the manifestation of your Lord's power. Matters are settled, and the Truth cannot be described as moving from place to place; how could He move about or travel, when He has no place or time, and no moment or duration applies to Him? For to be deprived of a moment regarding something means to miss the moments, and whoever misses something is incapable, whereas the Truth is far above having His attributes contained by natures or encompassed by hearts.

﴿And the angels come in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-Qarawi told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid told us, saying: 'Atiyyah told us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And on that Day Hell is brought near﴾, the color of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed and sweat appeared on his face, to the extent that what his companions saw of his condition weighed heavily upon them. Some of them went to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O 'Ali, something has happened which we have seen in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)." So 'Ali came, embraced him from behind, kissed between his shoulders, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, what has happened today and what has changed you?"

He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came and recited to me this verse: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near.﴾" I said: "How will it be brought?" He said: "Seventy thousand angels will bring it, leading it by seventy thousand bridles, and it will break loose with such a plunge that if it were left it would burn the people of the gathering. Then Hell will confront me and say: 'What is between me and you, O Muhammad? Allah has forbidden your flesh and blood to me.' No one will remain except that he says: 'myself, myself,' while Muhammad says: 'my nation, my nation.' Then Allah, glory be to Him, will say to the angels: 'Do you not see the people saying: "My Lord, myself, myself," while Muhammad says: "my nation, my nation"?'"[145] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/56.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: Hell will be led by seventy thousand *zamān* (chains or bridles), each bridle in the hand of seventy thousand angels; it will roar and groan until it is placed on the left of the Throne.

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say: "Would that I had sent ahead for my life"﴾, that is, for my life in the Hereafter. ﴿On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds.﴾ The majority read it with a *kasrah* on the *dhāl* and the *thā'* (*yu'adhdhibu* and *yūthiqu*), meaning: no one in this world punishes like Allah's punishment on that Day.

Al-Farra' said: it was also said that this refers to a specific man, Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. The meaning is: no one punishes like the punishment of this disbeliever, and no one binds like his binding. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this recitation, because:

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, saying: Hushaym and 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite, *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhabu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthaqu wathāqahu aḥad*, with the *dhāl* and *thā'* pronounced with a *fatḥah*.

It is also related that Abu 'Amr returned in the last part of his life to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The meaning of the verse is: no one among creation reaches the extent of Allah's punishment and binding, and that is the reference to the chains and the shackles.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhibu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥad*, meaning: "no one does to him."

﴿O soul at rest﴾, content with what Allah has promised, confirming what He has said.

Mujahid said: *al-munība* is the humble and submissive one who has become certain that Allah, glory be to Him, is our Lord, and who has steeled her heart for His command.

Al-Musayyib said: I heard al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq say: it is the one whose face Allah whitens, and to whom He gives her book in her right hand; then at that moment she is at rest. Al-Hasan said: the believing and certain one. 'Atiyyah said: the one content with Allah's decree. Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: the one safe from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/238.]]

'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari', who said: Hilal told me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hana'i, who said: in the recitation of Ubayy: *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-āminatu al-muṭma'innah* (O soul, secure and at rest).

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi informed me, saying: my father told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj told us, saying: Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*: he said: the one content with Allah's decree, who knows that what befell her would not have missed her, and that what missed her would not have befallen her. Ibn Kaysan said: the sincere one. Ibn 'Ata': she is the one who knows Allah, glory be to Him, and does not turn away from Him for the blink of an eye. It was also said: the one at rest through the remembrance of Allah. Its explanation is: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah﴾. It was also said: she is the one who trusts in Allah, exalted is He, and is confident in what He has guaranteed her of provision.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/57.]]

﴿Return to your Lord﴾. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse and the time of this saying. Some people said: it is said to her at death: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-'Askari told us, saying: al-'Ataridi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Return to your Lord, content and pleasing﴾: he said: this is at her departure from the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: ﴿Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Furati told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah told us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sulaymani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: When the believing servant dies, Allah, glory be to Him, sends two angels, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. It is said to her: "Come out, O soul at rest, come out to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is well pleased with you." She comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone ever smelled, and the angels are on the edges of the heaven.

They say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, a good breath." No gate is passed except that it is opened for her, and no angel except that he prays for her, until she is brought before the Merciful. Then the angels prostrate, and they say: "Our Lord, this is Your servant so-and-so, who used to worship You and never associated anything with You." He says: "Tell him to prostrate," and the soul prostrates. Then Mikail is called, and He says: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers until I ask you about her on the Day of Resurrection." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants grow for him in it. If he had any Qur'an with him, its light suffices him; if he did not, a likeness of the sun is made for him in his grave, and he is like a bride who sleeps, and no one wakes her except the dearest of her family to her, so she rises from her sleep as if she had not had enough of it. When the disbeliever dies, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends two angels and sends with them a piece of the most foul and rough cloth of every rough thing, and it is said: "O wicked soul, come out to scalding water and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: al-Masuhi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' al-Hanafi told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A man recited before the Prophet (ﷺ), *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*. Abu Bakr said: "How beautiful this is!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the angel will say it to you [at death]."[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/485, no. 35591; what is between brackets is from it.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Qasri informed us there, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari informed me. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Salim told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Munay' told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came, which was not seen in its form, and entered his bier, and then it was not seen leaving it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and the one reciting it was not seen: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, content and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.﴾

Others said: it is only said to her at the Resurrection: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, to your companion, your body. So Allah, glory be to Him, commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This view was held by 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and it is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as *fa-dkhulī fī 'abdī* ("enter among My servant"), with the monotheistic reading.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, those like you among the righteous servants of your Lord.

Some people of spiritual allusion said: ﴿O soul at rest﴾ in the world, ﴿return to Allah﴾ by leaving it; and returning to Allah is following the path of the Hereafter. ﴿Content﴾ with Allah in what He has prepared for her, ﴿pleasing﴾ to her Lord, who is pleased with her. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Some said: that is, with My servants, ﴿My Paradise﴾; the meaning of the verse involves inversion and reordering, and this was the view of Muqatil, al-Qurazi and Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And enter, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾, that is, with Our prophets in Paradise. Al-Akhfash said: that is, among My party. And another said: it is the command for the spirits to return to their bodies. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyyah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, regarding this verse, ﴿O soul at rest﴾, he said: it is the soul of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib; it was revealed concerning him on the day he was martyred at Uhud. Rather, his soul descended in the presence of the Lord of the worlds, honored and exalted above those near Him, until Allah, glory be to Him, returns it to Hamzah in tranquility, calm, and honor.

It was also revealed concerning Habib ibn 'Adi, whom the people of Makkah crucified and turned his face toward Madinah. He said: "O Allah, if I have any good with You, turn my face toward Your qibla." So Allah, glory be to Him, turned his face toward the qibla without anyone turning it, and no one could turn it. Its ruling is general for all believers who are at rest.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 15–30**

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and abundance﴾: that is, He tries him with blessing and plenty. ﴿He honors him with wealth and bestows on him favors through what He has widened for him, so he says: "My Lord has honored me,"﴾ and so he rejoices, is glad, praises Him for it and gives thanks. ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, measuring it out and straitening his sustenance, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me,"﴾ that is, has disgraced me with poverty. He does not thank Allah for what He has given him of soundness of limbs and the health and well-being He has provided. Qatadah said: "How quickly the son of Adam becomes ungrateful!"

The recitation of the majority is ﴿fa-qadara﴾ with a light *dal*. Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a doubled *dal* (*faqqadara*). Both are dialectal variants. Abu 'Amr used to say: *qadara* means *qattara* (to restrict), and *qaddara* means to give him what suffices him. Had it been the latter, he would not have said, "My Lord has humiliated me." Then He responded to him, saying: ﴿No!﴾ I did not test him with wealth because of his honor with Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his lowliness with Me. Poverty and wealth are part of My decree and My judgment. So I do not honor the one to whom I have given wealth and abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate the one whom I have humbled with poverty and scarcity of the world. Rather, I honor the one who honors Me by obedience, and I humiliate the one who humbles himself by disobedience to Me. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *kalla* (no) is that it is not fitting for him to be this way; rather, it is fitting that he praise Him for both circumstances, wealth and poverty.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honor the orphan﴾, meaning: I humiliated the one I humiliated because he does not honor the orphan.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The people of Basra read *yukrimūna* and what follows it entirely with the *yā'* (third person), while the others read it with the *tā'* (second person). ﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾: Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa read *tahāḍḍūna* with an *alif* and an open *tā'*. Al-Shadhhari related from al-Kisa'i *tuḥāḍḍūna* with a *ḍammah* on the *tā'*. Others read *taḥuḍḍūna* without the *alif*. ﴿And you devour the inheritance greedily﴾: *al-turāth* is the inheritance, and *aklan lamman* means intense, excessive eating. Al-Hasan said: he eats his own share and the share of others. Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *al-lamm* is transgression in inheritance; he consumes his own inheritance and that of others. Ibn Zayd said: *al-akl al-lamm* is the eating of one who devours everything he finds without asking whether it is lawful or unlawful, consuming what is his and what belongs to others. This was because they did not give inheritance to women or children. [The verse] ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾ and so on was recited. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, *lammtu mā 'alā al-khiwān* (I licked up what was on the tray), when one reaches what is on it and eats it all together.

﴿And you love wealth with an abundant love﴾: *jamman* means much, abundant. It is said *jamma al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ* (the water gathered in the basin) when it became abundant and collected. ﴿No!﴾ This is not how the matter ought to be. Then He informed about those who lament over what they have passed by, when it will no longer benefit them, saying, exalted is He who speaks:

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder﴾: meaning, repeatedly, time after time, so that everything upon it is crushed.

﴿And your Lord comes﴾: al-Hasan said: His command and His judgment. The people of spiritual allusion (*ahl al-ishārah*) said: the manifestation of your Lord's power. Matters are settled, and the Truth cannot be described as moving from place to place; how could He move about or travel, when He has no place or time, and no moment or duration applies to Him? For to be deprived of a moment regarding something means to miss the moments, and whoever misses something is incapable, whereas the Truth is far above having His attributes contained by natures or encompassed by hearts.

﴿And the angels come in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-Qarawi told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid told us, saying: 'Atiyyah told us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And on that Day Hell is brought near﴾, the color of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed and sweat appeared on his face, to the extent that what his companions saw of his condition weighed heavily upon them. Some of them went to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O 'Ali, something has happened which we have seen in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)." So 'Ali came, embraced him from behind, kissed between his shoulders, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, what has happened today and what has changed you?"

He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came and recited to me this verse: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near.﴾" I said: "How will it be brought?" He said: "Seventy thousand angels will bring it, leading it by seventy thousand bridles, and it will break loose with such a plunge that if it were left it would burn the people of the gathering. Then Hell will confront me and say: 'What is between me and you, O Muhammad? Allah has forbidden your flesh and blood to me.' No one will remain except that he says: 'myself, myself,' while Muhammad says: 'my nation, my nation.' Then Allah, glory be to Him, will say to the angels: 'Do you not see the people saying: "My Lord, myself, myself," while Muhammad says: "my nation, my nation"?'"[145] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/56.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: Hell will be led by seventy thousand *zamān* (chains or bridles), each bridle in the hand of seventy thousand angels; it will roar and groan until it is placed on the left of the Throne.

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say: "Would that I had sent ahead for my life"﴾, that is, for my life in the Hereafter. ﴿On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds.﴾ The majority read it with a *kasrah* on the *dhāl* and the *thā'* (*yu'adhdhibu* and *yūthiqu*), meaning: no one in this world punishes like Allah's punishment on that Day.

Al-Farra' said: it was also said that this refers to a specific man, Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. The meaning is: no one punishes like the punishment of this disbeliever, and no one binds like his binding. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this recitation, because:

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, saying: Hushaym and 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite, *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhabu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthaqu wathāqahu aḥad*, with the *dhāl* and *thā'* pronounced with a *fatḥah*.

It is also related that Abu 'Amr returned in the last part of his life to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The meaning of the verse is: no one among creation reaches the extent of Allah's punishment and binding, and that is the reference to the chains and the shackles.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhibu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥad*, meaning: "no one does to him."

﴿O soul at rest﴾, content with what Allah has promised, confirming what He has said.

Mujahid said: *al-munība* is the humble and submissive one who has become certain that Allah, glory be to Him, is our Lord, and who has steeled her heart for His command.

Al-Musayyib said: I heard al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq say: it is the one whose face Allah whitens, and to whom He gives her book in her right hand; then at that moment she is at rest. Al-Hasan said: the believing and certain one. 'Atiyyah said: the one content with Allah's decree. Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: the one safe from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/238.]]

'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari', who said: Hilal told me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hana'i, who said: in the recitation of Ubayy: *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-āminatu al-muṭma'innah* (O soul, secure and at rest).

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi informed me, saying: my father told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj told us, saying: Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*: he said: the one content with Allah's decree, who knows that what befell her would not have missed her, and that what missed her would not have befallen her. Ibn Kaysan said: the sincere one. Ibn 'Ata': she is the one who knows Allah, glory be to Him, and does not turn away from Him for the blink of an eye. It was also said: the one at rest through the remembrance of Allah. Its explanation is: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah﴾. It was also said: she is the one who trusts in Allah, exalted is He, and is confident in what He has guaranteed her of provision.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/57.]]

﴿Return to your Lord﴾. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse and the time of this saying. Some people said: it is said to her at death: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-'Askari told us, saying: al-'Ataridi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Return to your Lord, content and pleasing﴾: he said: this is at her departure from the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: ﴿Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Furati told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah told us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sulaymani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: When the believing servant dies, Allah, glory be to Him, sends two angels, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. It is said to her: "Come out, O soul at rest, come out to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is well pleased with you." She comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone ever smelled, and the angels are on the edges of the heaven.

They say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, a good breath." No gate is passed except that it is opened for her, and no angel except that he prays for her, until she is brought before the Merciful. Then the angels prostrate, and they say: "Our Lord, this is Your servant so-and-so, who used to worship You and never associated anything with You." He says: "Tell him to prostrate," and the soul prostrates. Then Mikail is called, and He says: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers until I ask you about her on the Day of Resurrection." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants grow for him in it. If he had any Qur'an with him, its light suffices him; if he did not, a likeness of the sun is made for him in his grave, and he is like a bride who sleeps, and no one wakes her except the dearest of her family to her, so she rises from her sleep as if she had not had enough of it. When the disbeliever dies, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends two angels and sends with them a piece of the most foul and rough cloth of every rough thing, and it is said: "O wicked soul, come out to scalding water and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: al-Masuhi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' al-Hanafi told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A man recited before the Prophet (ﷺ), *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*. Abu Bakr said: "How beautiful this is!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the angel will say it to you [at death]."[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/485, no. 35591; what is between brackets is from it.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Qasri informed us there, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari informed me. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Salim told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Munay' told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came, which was not seen in its form, and entered his bier, and then it was not seen leaving it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and the one reciting it was not seen: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, content and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.﴾

Others said: it is only said to her at the Resurrection: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, to your companion, your body. So Allah, glory be to Him, commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This view was held by 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and it is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as *fa-dkhulī fī 'abdī* ("enter among My servant"), with the monotheistic reading.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, those like you among the righteous servants of your Lord.

Some people of spiritual allusion said: ﴿O soul at rest﴾ in the world, ﴿return to Allah﴾ by leaving it; and returning to Allah is following the path of the Hereafter. ﴿Content﴾ with Allah in what He has prepared for her, ﴿pleasing﴾ to her Lord, who is pleased with her. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Some said: that is, with My servants, ﴿My Paradise﴾; the meaning of the verse involves inversion and reordering, and this was the view of Muqatil, al-Qurazi and Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And enter, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾, that is, with Our prophets in Paradise. Al-Akhfash said: that is, among My party. And another said: it is the command for the spirits to return to their bodies. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyyah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, regarding this verse, ﴿O soul at rest﴾, he said: it is the soul of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib; it was revealed concerning him on the day he was martyred at Uhud. Rather, his soul descended in the presence of the Lord of the worlds, honored and exalted above those near Him, until Allah, glory be to Him, returns it to Hamzah in tranquility, calm, and honor.

It was also revealed concerning Habib ibn 'Adi, whom the people of Makkah crucified and turned his face toward Madinah. He said: "O Allah, if I have any good with You, turn my face toward Your qibla." So Allah, glory be to Him, turned his face toward the qibla without anyone turning it, and no one could turn it. Its ruling is general for all believers who are at rest.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 15–30**

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and abundance﴾: that is, He tries him with blessing and plenty. ﴿He honors him with wealth and bestows on him favors through what He has widened for him, so he says: "My Lord has honored me,"﴾ and so he rejoices, is glad, praises Him for it and gives thanks. ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, measuring it out and straitening his sustenance, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me,"﴾ that is, has disgraced me with poverty. He does not thank Allah for what He has given him of soundness of limbs and the health and well-being He has provided. Qatadah said: "How quickly the son of Adam becomes ungrateful!"

The recitation of the majority is ﴿fa-qadara﴾ with a light *dal*. Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a doubled *dal* (*faqqadara*). Both are dialectal variants. Abu 'Amr used to say: *qadara* means *qattara* (to restrict), and *qaddara* means to give him what suffices him. Had it been the latter, he would not have said, "My Lord has humiliated me." Then He responded to him, saying: ﴿No!﴾ I did not test him with wealth because of his honor with Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his lowliness with Me. Poverty and wealth are part of My decree and My judgment. So I do not honor the one to whom I have given wealth and abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate the one whom I have humbled with poverty and scarcity of the world. Rather, I honor the one who honors Me by obedience, and I humiliate the one who humbles himself by disobedience to Me. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *kalla* (no) is that it is not fitting for him to be this way; rather, it is fitting that he praise Him for both circumstances, wealth and poverty.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honor the orphan﴾, meaning: I humiliated the one I humiliated because he does not honor the orphan.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The people of Basra read *yukrimūna* and what follows it entirely with the *yā'* (third person), while the others read it with the *tā'* (second person). ﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾: Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa read *tahāḍḍūna* with an *alif* and an open *tā'*. Al-Shadhhari related from al-Kisa'i *tuḥāḍḍūna* with a *ḍammah* on the *tā'*. Others read *taḥuḍḍūna* without the *alif*. ﴿And you devour the inheritance greedily﴾: *al-turāth* is the inheritance, and *aklan lamman* means intense, excessive eating. Al-Hasan said: he eats his own share and the share of others. Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *al-lamm* is transgression in inheritance; he consumes his own inheritance and that of others. Ibn Zayd said: *al-akl al-lamm* is the eating of one who devours everything he finds without asking whether it is lawful or unlawful, consuming what is his and what belongs to others. This was because they did not give inheritance to women or children. [The verse] ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾ and so on was recited. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, *lammtu mā 'alā al-khiwān* (I licked up what was on the tray), when one reaches what is on it and eats it all together.

﴿And you love wealth with an abundant love﴾: *jamman* means much, abundant. It is said *jamma al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ* (the water gathered in the basin) when it became abundant and collected. ﴿No!﴾ This is not how the matter ought to be. Then He informed about those who lament over what they have passed by, when it will no longer benefit them, saying, exalted is He who speaks:

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder﴾: meaning, repeatedly, time after time, so that everything upon it is crushed.

﴿And your Lord comes﴾: al-Hasan said: His command and His judgment. The people of spiritual allusion (*ahl al-ishārah*) said: the manifestation of your Lord's power. Matters are settled, and the Truth cannot be described as moving from place to place; how could He move about or travel, when He has no place or time, and no moment or duration applies to Him? For to be deprived of a moment regarding something means to miss the moments, and whoever misses something is incapable, whereas the Truth is far above having His attributes contained by natures or encompassed by hearts.

﴿And the angels come in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-Qarawi told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid told us, saying: 'Atiyyah told us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And on that Day Hell is brought near﴾, the color of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed and sweat appeared on his face, to the extent that what his companions saw of his condition weighed heavily upon them. Some of them went to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O 'Ali, something has happened which we have seen in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)." So 'Ali came, embraced him from behind, kissed between his shoulders, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, what has happened today and what has changed you?"

He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came and recited to me this verse: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near.﴾" I said: "How will it be brought?" He said: "Seventy thousand angels will bring it, leading it by seventy thousand bridles, and it will break loose with such a plunge that if it were left it would burn the people of the gathering. Then Hell will confront me and say: 'What is between me and you, O Muhammad? Allah has forbidden your flesh and blood to me.' No one will remain except that he says: 'myself, myself,' while Muhammad says: 'my nation, my nation.' Then Allah, glory be to Him, will say to the angels: 'Do you not see the people saying: "My Lord, myself, myself," while Muhammad says: "my nation, my nation"?'"[145] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/56.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: Hell will be led by seventy thousand *zamān* (chains or bridles), each bridle in the hand of seventy thousand angels; it will roar and groan until it is placed on the left of the Throne.

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say: "Would that I had sent ahead for my life"﴾, that is, for my life in the Hereafter. ﴿On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds.﴾ The majority read it with a *kasrah* on the *dhāl* and the *thā'* (*yu'adhdhibu* and *yūthiqu*), meaning: no one in this world punishes like Allah's punishment on that Day.

Al-Farra' said: it was also said that this refers to a specific man, Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. The meaning is: no one punishes like the punishment of this disbeliever, and no one binds like his binding. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this recitation, because:

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, saying: Hushaym and 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite, *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhabu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthaqu wathāqahu aḥad*, with the *dhāl* and *thā'* pronounced with a *fatḥah*.

It is also related that Abu 'Amr returned in the last part of his life to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The meaning of the verse is: no one among creation reaches the extent of Allah's punishment and binding, and that is the reference to the chains and the shackles.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhibu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥad*, meaning: "no one does to him."

﴿O soul at rest﴾, content with what Allah has promised, confirming what He has said.

Mujahid said: *al-munība* is the humble and submissive one who has become certain that Allah, glory be to Him, is our Lord, and who has steeled her heart for His command.

Al-Musayyib said: I heard al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq say: it is the one whose face Allah whitens, and to whom He gives her book in her right hand; then at that moment she is at rest. Al-Hasan said: the believing and certain one. 'Atiyyah said: the one content with Allah's decree. Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: the one safe from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/238.]]

'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari', who said: Hilal told me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hana'i, who said: in the recitation of Ubayy: *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-āminatu al-muṭma'innah* (O soul, secure and at rest).

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi informed me, saying: my father told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj told us, saying: Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*: he said: the one content with Allah's decree, who knows that what befell her would not have missed her, and that what missed her would not have befallen her. Ibn Kaysan said: the sincere one. Ibn 'Ata': she is the one who knows Allah, glory be to Him, and does not turn away from Him for the blink of an eye. It was also said: the one at rest through the remembrance of Allah. Its explanation is: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah﴾. It was also said: she is the one who trusts in Allah, exalted is He, and is confident in what He has guaranteed her of provision.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/57.]]

﴿Return to your Lord﴾. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse and the time of this saying. Some people said: it is said to her at death: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-'Askari told us, saying: al-'Ataridi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Return to your Lord, content and pleasing﴾: he said: this is at her departure from the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: ﴿Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Furati told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah told us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sulaymani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: When the believing servant dies, Allah, glory be to Him, sends two angels, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. It is said to her: "Come out, O soul at rest, come out to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is well pleased with you." She comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone ever smelled, and the angels are on the edges of the heaven.

They say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, a good breath." No gate is passed except that it is opened for her, and no angel except that he prays for her, until she is brought before the Merciful. Then the angels prostrate, and they say: "Our Lord, this is Your servant so-and-so, who used to worship You and never associated anything with You." He says: "Tell him to prostrate," and the soul prostrates. Then Mikail is called, and He says: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers until I ask you about her on the Day of Resurrection." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants grow for him in it. If he had any Qur'an with him, its light suffices him; if he did not, a likeness of the sun is made for him in his grave, and he is like a bride who sleeps, and no one wakes her except the dearest of her family to her, so she rises from her sleep as if she had not had enough of it. When the disbeliever dies, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends two angels and sends with them a piece of the most foul and rough cloth of every rough thing, and it is said: "O wicked soul, come out to scalding water and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: al-Masuhi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' al-Hanafi told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A man recited before the Prophet (ﷺ), *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*. Abu Bakr said: "How beautiful this is!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the angel will say it to you [at death]."[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/485, no. 35591; what is between brackets is from it.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Qasri informed us there, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari informed me. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Salim told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Munay' told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came, which was not seen in its form, and entered his bier, and then it was not seen leaving it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and the one reciting it was not seen: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, content and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.﴾

Others said: it is only said to her at the Resurrection: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, to your companion, your body. So Allah, glory be to Him, commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This view was held by 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and it is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as *fa-dkhulī fī 'abdī* ("enter among My servant"), with the monotheistic reading.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, those like you among the righteous servants of your Lord.

Some people of spiritual allusion said: ﴿O soul at rest﴾ in the world, ﴿return to Allah﴾ by leaving it; and returning to Allah is following the path of the Hereafter. ﴿Content﴾ with Allah in what He has prepared for her, ﴿pleasing﴾ to her Lord, who is pleased with her. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Some said: that is, with My servants, ﴿My Paradise﴾; the meaning of the verse involves inversion and reordering, and this was the view of Muqatil, al-Qurazi and Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And enter, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾, that is, with Our prophets in Paradise. Al-Akhfash said: that is, among My party. And another said: it is the command for the spirits to return to their bodies. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyyah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, regarding this verse, ﴿O soul at rest﴾, he said: it is the soul of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib; it was revealed concerning him on the day he was martyred at Uhud. Rather, his soul descended in the presence of the Lord of the worlds, honored and exalted above those near Him, until Allah, glory be to Him, returns it to Hamzah in tranquility, calm, and honor.

It was also revealed concerning Habib ibn 'Adi, whom the people of Makkah crucified and turned his face toward Madinah. He said: "O Allah, if I have any good with You, turn my face toward Your qibla." So Allah, glory be to Him, turned his face toward the qibla without anyone turning it, and no one could turn it. Its ruling is general for all believers who are at rest.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 15–30**

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and abundance﴾: that is, He tries him with blessing and plenty. ﴿He honors him with wealth and bestows on him favors through what He has widened for him, so he says: "My Lord has honored me,"﴾ and so he rejoices, is glad, praises Him for it and gives thanks. ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, measuring it out and straitening his sustenance, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me,"﴾ that is, has disgraced me with poverty. He does not thank Allah for what He has given him of soundness of limbs and the health and well-being He has provided. Qatadah said: "How quickly the son of Adam becomes ungrateful!"

The recitation of the majority is ﴿fa-qadara﴾ with a light *dal*. Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a doubled *dal* (*faqqadara*). Both are dialectal variants. Abu 'Amr used to say: *qadara* means *qattara* (to restrict), and *qaddara* means to give him what suffices him. Had it been the latter, he would not have said, "My Lord has humiliated me." Then He responded to him, saying: ﴿No!﴾ I did not test him with wealth because of his honor with Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his lowliness with Me. Poverty and wealth are part of My decree and My judgment. So I do not honor the one to whom I have given wealth and abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate the one whom I have humbled with poverty and scarcity of the world. Rather, I honor the one who honors Me by obedience, and I humiliate the one who humbles himself by disobedience to Me. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *kalla* (no) is that it is not fitting for him to be this way; rather, it is fitting that he praise Him for both circumstances, wealth and poverty.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honor the orphan﴾, meaning: I humiliated the one I humiliated because he does not honor the orphan.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The people of Basra read *yukrimūna* and what follows it entirely with the *yā'* (third person), while the others read it with the *tā'* (second person). ﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾: Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa read *tahāḍḍūna* with an *alif* and an open *tā'*. Al-Shadhhari related from al-Kisa'i *tuḥāḍḍūna* with a *ḍammah* on the *tā'*. Others read *taḥuḍḍūna* without the *alif*. ﴿And you devour the inheritance greedily﴾: *al-turāth* is the inheritance, and *aklan lamman* means intense, excessive eating. Al-Hasan said: he eats his own share and the share of others. Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *al-lamm* is transgression in inheritance; he consumes his own inheritance and that of others. Ibn Zayd said: *al-akl al-lamm* is the eating of one who devours everything he finds without asking whether it is lawful or unlawful, consuming what is his and what belongs to others. This was because they did not give inheritance to women or children. [The verse] ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾ and so on was recited. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, *lammtu mā 'alā al-khiwān* (I licked up what was on the tray), when one reaches what is on it and eats it all together.

﴿And you love wealth with an abundant love﴾: *jamman* means much, abundant. It is said *jamma al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ* (the water gathered in the basin) when it became abundant and collected. ﴿No!﴾ This is not how the matter ought to be. Then He informed about those who lament over what they have passed by, when it will no longer benefit them, saying, exalted is He who speaks:

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder﴾: meaning, repeatedly, time after time, so that everything upon it is crushed.

﴿And your Lord comes﴾: al-Hasan said: His command and His judgment. The people of spiritual allusion (*ahl al-ishārah*) said: the manifestation of your Lord's power. Matters are settled, and the Truth cannot be described as moving from place to place; how could He move about or travel, when He has no place or time, and no moment or duration applies to Him? For to be deprived of a moment regarding something means to miss the moments, and whoever misses something is incapable, whereas the Truth is far above having His attributes contained by natures or encompassed by hearts.

﴿And the angels come in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-Qarawi told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid told us, saying: 'Atiyyah told us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And on that Day Hell is brought near﴾, the color of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed and sweat appeared on his face, to the extent that what his companions saw of his condition weighed heavily upon them. Some of them went to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O 'Ali, something has happened which we have seen in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)." So 'Ali came, embraced him from behind, kissed between his shoulders, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, what has happened today and what has changed you?"

He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came and recited to me this verse: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near.﴾" I said: "How will it be brought?" He said: "Seventy thousand angels will bring it, leading it by seventy thousand bridles, and it will break loose with such a plunge that if it were left it would burn the people of the gathering. Then Hell will confront me and say: 'What is between me and you, O Muhammad? Allah has forbidden your flesh and blood to me.' No one will remain except that he says: 'myself, myself,' while Muhammad says: 'my nation, my nation.' Then Allah, glory be to Him, will say to the angels: 'Do you not see the people saying: "My Lord, myself, myself," while Muhammad says: "my nation, my nation"?'"[145] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/56.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: Hell will be led by seventy thousand *zamān* (chains or bridles), each bridle in the hand of seventy thousand angels; it will roar and groan until it is placed on the left of the Throne.

﴿On that Day man will remember, but how will the reminder benefit him?﴾ ﴿He will say: "Would that I had sent ahead for my life"﴾, that is, for my life in the Hereafter. ﴿On that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds.﴾ The majority read it with a *kasrah* on the *dhāl* and the *thā'* (*yu'adhdhibu* and *yūthiqu*), meaning: no one in this world punishes like Allah's punishment on that Day.

Al-Farra' said: it was also said that this refers to a specific man, Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi. The meaning is: no one punishes like the punishment of this disbeliever, and no one binds like his binding. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this recitation, because:

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, saying: Hushaym and 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had taught to recite, *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhabu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthaqu wathāqahu aḥad*, with the *dhāl* and *thā'* pronounced with a *fatḥah*.

It is also related that Abu 'Amr returned in the last part of his life to the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ).

The meaning of the verse is: no one among creation reaches the extent of Allah's punishment and binding, and that is the reference to the chains and the shackles.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying:

Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from one who heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite *fa-yawma'idhin lā yu'adhdhibu 'adhābahu aḥadun wa lā yūthiqu wathāqahu aḥad*, meaning: "no one does to him."

﴿O soul at rest﴾, content with what Allah has promised, confirming what He has said.

Mujahid said: *al-munība* is the humble and submissive one who has become certain that Allah, glory be to Him, is our Lord, and who has steeled her heart for His command.

Al-Musayyib said: I heard al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq say: it is the one whose face Allah whitens, and to whom He gives her book in her right hand; then at that moment she is at rest. Al-Hasan said: the believing and certain one. 'Atiyyah said: the one content with Allah's decree. Hayyan, from al-Kalbi: the one safe from the punishment of Allah, exalted is He.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/238.]]

'Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Khallad ibn Aslam told us, saying: al-Nadr informed us, from Harun al-Qari', who said: Hilal told me, from Abu Shaykh al-Hana'i, who said: in the recitation of Ubayy: *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-āminatu al-muṭma'innah* (O soul, secure and at rest).

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Sha'bi informed me, saying: my father told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Siraj told us, saying: Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, from Ibrahim ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*: he said: the one content with Allah's decree, who knows that what befell her would not have missed her, and that what missed her would not have befallen her. Ibn Kaysan said: the sincere one. Ibn 'Ata': she is the one who knows Allah, glory be to Him, and does not turn away from Him for the blink of an eye. It was also said: the one at rest through the remembrance of Allah. Its explanation is: ﴿and their hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah﴾. It was also said: she is the one who trusts in Allah, exalted is He, and is confident in what He has guaranteed her of provision.[[See Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/57.]]

﴿Return to your Lord﴾. The scholars differed in interpreting this verse and the time of this saying. Some people said: it is said to her at death: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, who is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Samurah al-Baghawi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sahl al-'Askari told us, saying: al-'Ataridi told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' told us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Return to your Lord, content and pleasing﴾: he said: this is at her departure from the world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: ﴿Enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: al-Furati told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid told us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah told us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sulaymani, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: When the believing servant dies, Allah, glory be to Him, sends two angels, and sends to him a gift from Paradise. It is said to her: "Come out, O soul at rest, come out to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is well pleased with you." She comes out like the finest scent of musk that anyone ever smelled, and the angels are on the edges of the heaven.

They say: "A good spirit has come from the earth, a good breath." No gate is passed except that it is opened for her, and no angel except that he prays for her, until she is brought before the Merciful. Then the angels prostrate, and they say: "Our Lord, this is Your servant so-and-so, who used to worship You and never associated anything with You." He says: "Tell him to prostrate," and the soul prostrates. Then Mikail is called, and He says: "Take her and place her with the souls of the believers until I ask you about her on the Day of Resurrection." Then he is commanded, and his grave is widened for him seventy cubits in width and seventy cubits in length, and fragrant plants grow for him in it. If he had any Qur'an with him, its light suffices him; if he did not, a likeness of the sun is made for him in his grave, and he is like a bride who sleeps, and no one wakes her except the dearest of her family to her, so she rises from her sleep as if she had not had enough of it. When the disbeliever dies, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends two angels and sends with them a piece of the most foul and rough cloth of every rough thing, and it is said: "O wicked soul, come out to scalding water and painful punishment, and your Lord is angry with you."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan told us, saying: al-Masuhi told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' al-Hanafi told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A man recited before the Prophet (ﷺ), *yā ayyatuhā al-nafs al-muṭma'innah*. Abu Bakr said: "How beautiful this is!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the angel will say it to you [at death]."[[Kanz al-'Ummal: 12/485, no. 35591; what is between brackets is from it.]]

Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Qasri informed us there, saying: Isma'il ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us in Baghdad, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, saying: Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari informed me. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Salim told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Munay' told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came, which was not seen in its form, and entered his bier, and then it was not seen leaving it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, and the one reciting it was not seen: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, content and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Paradise.﴾

Others said: it is only said to her at the Resurrection: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, to your companion, your body. So Allah, glory be to Him, commands the spirits to return to the bodies. This view was held by 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and it is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

The evidence for this interpretation is what Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Harun, from Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited it as *fa-dkhulī fī 'abdī* ("enter among My servant"), with the monotheistic reading.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: return to the reward of your Lord and His honor. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿Return to your Lord﴾, that is, those like you among the righteous servants of your Lord.

Some people of spiritual allusion said: ﴿O soul at rest﴾ in the world, ﴿return to Allah﴾ by leaving it; and returning to Allah is following the path of the Hereafter. ﴿Content﴾ with Allah in what He has prepared for her, ﴿pleasing﴾ to her Lord, who is pleased with her. ﴿So enter among My servants﴾. Some said: that is, with My servants, ﴿My Paradise﴾; the meaning of the verse involves inversion and reordering, and this was the view of Muqatil, al-Qurazi and Abu 'Ubaydah. ﴿And enter, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾, that is, with Our prophets in Paradise. Al-Akhfash said: that is, among My party. And another said: it is the command for the spirits to return to their bodies. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad told us, saying: Ibn 'Alawiyyah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: al-Musayyib told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Buraydah, regarding this verse, ﴿O soul at rest﴾, he said: it is the soul of Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib; it was revealed concerning him on the day he was martyred at Uhud. Rather, his soul descended in the presence of the Lord of the worlds, honored and exalted above those near Him, until Allah, glory be to Him, returns it to Hamzah in tranquility, calm, and honor.

It was also revealed concerning Habib ibn 'Adi, whom the people of Makkah crucified and turned his face toward Madinah. He said: "O Allah, if I have any good with You, turn my face toward Your qibla." So Allah, glory be to Him, turned his face toward the qibla without anyone turning it, and no one could turn it. Its ruling is general for all believers who are at rest.

**Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 89, verses 15–30**

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him by giving him honor and abundance﴾: that is, He tries him with blessing and plenty. ﴿He honors him with wealth and bestows on him favors through what He has widened for him, so he says: "My Lord has honored me,"﴾ and so he rejoices, is glad, praises Him for it and gives thanks. ﴿But when He tests him by restricting his provision, measuring it out and straitening his sustenance, he says: "My Lord has humiliated me,"﴾ that is, has disgraced me with poverty. He does not thank Allah for what He has given him of soundness of limbs and the health and well-being He has provided. Qatadah said: "How quickly the son of Adam becomes ungrateful!"

The recitation of the majority is ﴿fa-qadara﴾ with a light *dal*. Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read it with a doubled *dal* (*faqqadara*). Both are dialectal variants. Abu 'Amr used to say: *qadara* means *qattara* (to restrict), and *qaddara* means to give him what suffices him. Had it been the latter, he would not have said, "My Lord has humiliated me." Then He responded to him, saying: ﴿No!﴾ I did not test him with wealth because of his honor with Me, nor did I test him with poverty because of his lowliness with Me. Poverty and wealth are part of My decree and My judgment. So I do not honor the one to whom I have given wealth and abundance of the world, nor do I humiliate the one whom I have humbled with poverty and scarcity of the world. Rather, I honor the one who honors Me by obedience, and I humiliate the one who humbles himself by disobedience to Me. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of *kalla* (no) is that it is not fitting for him to be this way; rather, it is fitting that he praise Him for both circumstances, wealth and poverty.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, but you do not honor the orphan﴾, meaning: I humiliated the one I humiliated because he does not honor the orphan.

The reciters differed regarding this verse. The people of Basra read *yukrimūna* and what follows it entirely with the *yā'* (third person), while the others read it with the *tā'* (second person). ﴿And you do not urge one another to feed the needy﴾: Abu Ja'far and the people of Kufa read *tahāḍḍūna* with an *alif* and an open *tā'*. Al-Shadhhari related from al-Kisa'i *tuḥāḍḍūna* with a *ḍammah* on the *tā'*. Others read *taḥuḍḍūna* without the *alif*. ﴿And you devour the inheritance greedily﴾: *al-turāth* is the inheritance, and *aklan lamman* means intense, excessive eating. Al-Hasan said: he eats his own share and the share of others. Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: *al-lamm* is transgression in inheritance; he consumes his own inheritance and that of others. Ibn Zayd said: *al-akl al-lamm* is the eating of one who devours everything he finds without asking whether it is lawful or unlawful, consuming what is his and what belongs to others. This was because they did not give inheritance to women or children. [The verse] ﴿They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾ and so on was recited. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said, *lammtu mā 'alā al-khiwān* (I licked up what was on the tray), when one reaches what is on it and eats it all together.

﴿And you love wealth with an abundant love﴾: *jamman* means much, abundant. It is said *jamma al-mā' fī al-ḥawḍ* (the water gathered in the basin) when it became abundant and collected. ﴿No!﴾ This is not how the matter ought to be. Then He informed about those who lament over what they have passed by, when it will no longer benefit them, saying, exalted is He who speaks:

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder﴾: meaning, repeatedly, time after time, so that everything upon it is crushed.

﴿And your Lord comes﴾: al-Hasan said: His command and His judgment. The people of spiritual allusion (*ahl al-ishārah*) said: the manifestation of your Lord's power. Matters are settled, and the Truth cannot be described as moving from place to place; how could He move about or travel, when He has no place or time, and no moment or duration applies to Him? For to be deprived of a moment regarding something means to miss the moments, and whoever misses something is incapable, whereas the Truth is far above having His attributes contained by natures or encompassed by hearts.

﴿And the angels come in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near﴾.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Majah told us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-Qarawi told us, saying: al-Qasim ibn al-Hakam told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid told us, saying: 'Atiyyah told us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And on that Day Hell is brought near﴾, the color of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed and sweat appeared on his face, to the extent that what his companions saw of his condition weighed heavily upon them. Some of them went to 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O 'Ali, something has happened which we have seen in the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ)." So 'Ali came, embraced him from behind, kissed between his shoulders, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, what has happened today and what has changed you?"

He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came and recited to me this verse: ﴿No! When the earth is pounded to powder, powder upon powder, and your Lord comes, and the angels in ranks, rank upon rank, and on that Day Hell is brought near.﴾" I said: "How will it be brought?" He said: "Seventy thousand angels will bring it, leading it by seventy thousand bridles, and it will break loose with such a plunge that if it were left it would burn the people of the gathering. Then Hell will confront me and say: 'What is between me and you, O Muhammad? Allah has forbidden your flesh and blood to me.' No one will remain except that he says: 'myself, myself,' while Muhammad says: 'my nation, my nation.' Then Allah, glory be to Him, will say to the angels: 'Do you not see the people saying: "My Lord, myself, myself," while Muhammad says: "my nation, my nation"?'"[145] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/56.]]

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Muqatil said regarding this verse: Hell will be led by seventy thousand *zamān* (chains or bridles), each bridle in the hand of seventy thousand angels; it will roar and groan until it is placed on the left of the Throne.
